metadata.title: Locally finite p-groups in Golod groups and an AT section
metadata.description:
We give an affirmative answer to Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.131 of A. V. Timofeenko. For every prime p, we construct a countable infinite locally finite AT p-group satisfying Rozhkov's original infinite-support definition and an epimorphism onto it from a subgroup of a classical homogeneous, residually finite Golod p-group. More generally, every countably infinite locally finite p-group embeds in a Golod group in the precise canonical nil-adjoint sense of Problem 9.76, and is a quotient of a subgroup of such a classical homogeneous Golod group.

The argument uses the established stable-nil embedding construction of Alahmadi, Alsulami, Jain and Zelmanov, first published in 2017. Relative elementary matrices place the needed unit derived subgroup in a finitely generated canonical adjoint subgroup. A direct scalar-extension argument gives absolute nilness for the selected realization, allowing Hammoudi's homogeneous Golod cover to be applied. The AT target is infinitely generated; no answer to Problem 13.55 or finitely generated AT-target strengthening is claimed.

The seven-page note is accompanied by LaTeX source, standard-library exact verifiers, expected outputs, source and priority audits, and independent AI adversarial reviews. Finite computations supplement the infinite proofs and do not certify their universal quantifiers. The extensive bounded literature search through 24 October 2026 found no earlier complete same-scope result; this is not an exhaustive certification of first priority. Original 1986 AT text was inspected through primary indexed full text; its PDF bytes were not acquired. AI tools were used extensively in discovery, development, writing and verification. This preprint has not undergone independent human peer review, and no formal proof-assistant verification is claimed. Paper, prose and code: CC BY 4.0.

metadata.title: A sharp forest bound and an improved whisker bound for finite WARM graphs
metadata.description:
For power reinforcement on a finite simple undirected loopless graph, the infinitely reinforced edges almost surely form a forest for alpha > 4/3, for arbitrary positive vertex firing rates and arbitrary fixed positive integer initial counts. The known unit triangle obstruction shows that the strict forest constant cannot be decreased. For equal rates every surviving component is a tree of diameter at most three for alpha >= 17/4. The stochastic equality endpoint alpha = 4/3 and the suggested sharper whisker interval remain unresolved.

The deterministic contribution is an arbitrary-equilibrium weighted odd-cycle instability bound alpha > sec^2(pi/(2m)), robust under unequal rates, chords and attachments, together with exact scalar interval and unbounded-tail estimates for whiskers. Published finite stochastic convergence/support results, the even-cycle method, the uniform odd-cycle spectrum, triangle obstruction, and least-weight/champion arguments are explicitly credited. The earlier published proof already implies the weaker whisker bound alpha >= 24; the manuscript records a conservative strict version and its exact bridge. The forest result answers the finite forest-bound improvement requested by Kleptsyn in OWR12/2023 printed655 (30005455 / OWR-12697708-008).

Two independently derived bounded priority investigations recovered no earlier theorem giving either substantive universal bound. This is not an exhaustive priority, global openness, first discovery or historical public-visibility certificate. The companion archive preserves the eight original submitted artifacts, the complete source, separate mathematical and priority audits, exact rational finite controls, complete expected outputs and a portable offline runner. Historical partial labels are explicitly reconciled with the literal requests and the stronger unresolved sharpness suggestion. Computations supplement the universal proof; hashes establish custody rather than mathematics.

AI tools were extensively involved in mathematical research, proof development, symbolic and computational verification, adversarial auditing, literature investigation and manuscript preparation. This manuscript and supporting materials are unrefereed. Internal AI reviews are not formal independent human peer review, journal acceptance or proof-assistant certification.

metadata.title: A free-chain counterexample to a Nash-intersection conjecture
metadata.description:
For the complete family of prime divisors obtained by n successive free point blowups over the smooth complex surface germ, fixing a prefix of k centers with 2 <= k < n gives the closed Nash-set intersection {ord x >= ceil(n/k), ord y >= n}. Five blowups give thresholds (3,5) and (2,5) when two or three centers are fixed. Neither is q(1,j) for any positive integers q,j, so no positive contact multiple of any reference prefix divisor equals the intersection. The proof exhausts all complex free-center choices and treats both charts, satellite limits, identically zero x, constant arcs, exact/at-least contact closures and all integer multiplicities. Explicit separating arcs are nonconstant convergent polynomials.

This is a negative answer to the specified-reference-multiple assertion of Conjecture 1 in Fernandez de Bobadilla, Pe Pereira and Popescu-Pampu, arXiv1501.06898v3 p.31, and Pe Pereira's joint OWR46/2016 contribution p.2679, under every contact/index convention explicitly mapped in the paper. In particular fixing the genuinely free selected c3 still leaves c4,c5 variable. The source uses an intersection; a catalogue union is a transcription discrepancy. Its bare equivalence symbol is undefined and its global indexing inconsistent, so no unique author-intended correction or unspecified replacement is asserted. The intersections ARE maximal divisorial sets for other primitive toric weights; no arbitrary-divisor negative, nonreduced-scheme equality, Conjecture 2 or general Nash-problem solution is claimed.

The standard divisorial/contact and toric framework, and the original paper's combinatorial invariance and cylindrical intersection results, are explicitly credited. The contribution is the complete free-family calculation and reference-ray obstruction. A bounded extensive primary-source investigation found no authenticated earlier exact negative calculation; no exhaustive novelty, historical firstness or continuous-open-status certificate is claimed. Actual arXiv/workshop bodies and selected older/new primary theorems were read; the publisher-typeset original body remains inaccessible403. The proof was already public in PR1332 before this note; the present version is dated22October2026 and is not backdated.

The proposed deposit contains the five-page paper and complete editable-source/verification ZIP. New standard-library exact diagnostics supplement the universal written proof and named standard background; no independent replay of unavailable claimant programs or proof-assistant certification is claimed. metadata.title: A singleton-supported cycle correction to Byrnes's differential-poset bound
metadata.description:
For every ordinary unweighted r-differential poset and n at least 2, an explicit nonnegative singleton-supported cycle rank q_n is subtracted from Byrnes's cumulative upper bound. The correction depends only on the two preceding incidence ranks. Terminal-preserving witness trees prove the cycle transfer b_n at least q_n. Standard reflected Young-prefix examples attain strict improvements from 31 to 30 for r=3 and from 20 to 19 for r=1, making coefficient one sharp. A singleton-successor sufficient condition, conditional two-witness equality characterization and the all-r rank-three consequence are proved.

This answers Majumder's printed request for an improvement of the Byrnes inequality in an incidence-dependent form. Stanley's general local recurrence, the separate combinatorial strict-growth-proof question and improvement of the global Fibonacci envelope are not claimed. Classical incidence identities, graph facts, singleton methods and Wagner reflection are credited. Gaetz-Venkataramana Proposition 3.4 already gives the exact rank-one two-singleton lemma used in the rank-three deduction; the witness poset families are standard. A dated bounded primary-source comparison found no earlier equivalent supported-cycle upper-bound theorem in inspected material; historical firstness, a new general method and present worldwide openness are not certified.

The deposit consists of a seven-page paper and a complete editable-source/verification ZIP, preserving all eight original submitted artifacts. Portable standard-library exact checks, complete expected outputs, closed manifests and a local rebuild script are included. Finite computations supplement the written universal proof and do not certify full recurrence or literature absence. metadata.title: Logarithmic Bray sampling in symplectic and orthogonal groups
metadata.description:
For every odd prime-power field order q and all sufficiently large natural dimensions n, for every actual fixed strong involution t in Sp(V), O(V), SO(V) or Ω(V), each separately specified t-eigenspace has probability at least c/log n of receiving a strong restriction of the even Bray output inv(tt^g), with g independent and uniformly distributed in the actual group. On a d-dimensional space, strong means both eigenspace dimensions lie in the closed interval [d/3, 2d/3].

The manuscript proves unconditional graph-chart masses for self-adjoint operators, all four orthogonal determinant-character sectors including q=3 and zero-dimensional complements, and an exact half-mass square-spinor refinement. A 192-prescribed-class generation argument using the stated published Burness and Liebeck–Pyber–Shalev results, together with a natural-central-cover and simple-quotient graph argument using 385 disjoint first-success blocks, shows that O(log n·(1+log(1/δ))) independent uniform samples generate a subgroup containing C_G(t)′′ with probability at least 1−δ, for every 0<δ<1.

This addresses the symplectic and orthogonal parts of the fixed-strong-involution Bray sampling problem reported in Oberwolfach Report37/2016, pp2160–2161 (repository problem30003185, PR1330). The linear and unitary marginal/generation results are existing work of Dixon–Praeger–Seress and Glasby–Praeger–Roney-Dougal; their distinguished2-part method and independent diagonal-escape strategy are credited. The 2026 stingray random-power construction has a different target. Bounded priority comparisons do not establish global firstness.

The theorem is asymptotic in natural dimension and concerns sample count at prescribed confidence. It makes no all-dimension, characteristic-two, projective-involution, order-four-lift, similitude or total-running-time assertion, and no claim that a fixed multiplier gives vanishing error. Sp4 zero marginal and arbitrarily large 2:1 non-simultaneous-strength obstructions are explained. The two eigenspace events are separate, not a simultaneous bound.

The deposit contains the paper PDF and a source-and-verification archive with complete editable proofs, exact standard-library finite diagnostics and expected results, dependency and priority limits, provenance, licenses, a source manifest and an offline deterministic packaging builder. Finite diagnostics corroborate selected interfaces and do not prove universal mathematics. No third-party article/book body, account capture or operational service tool is distributed.

AI tools were extensively involved in the mathematical research, proof development, computational verification, manuscript preparation and auditing. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not undergone formal independent human peer review.

metadata.title: NP-completeness of the initial odd-ear prefix
metadata.description:
The variable-threshold decision problem beta(G)>=t for the maximum initial consecutive odd prefix of an open ear decomposition is NP-complete, even on finite simple 2-vertex-connected graphs with a universal vertex whose deletion leaves a connected bipartite graph. The initial circuit and one-edge ears are counted; the first even ear ends the prefix. This gives a full complexity answer to Sebo's OWR 2014 Question 4 and Benchetrit-Sebo's 2015 Question 3.3. It does not assert P!=NP, fixed-threshold hardness, closed-ear hardness or a theorem about the total number of odd ears.

The six-page note combines the classical factor-critical formulation with an explicit cone identity and a polynomial Set Cover reduction. Complete proofs include all preprocessing branches within the cone subclass, private-element perfect matchings, arbitrary partial blocks and omitted distinguished vertices, the exact loss identity d_i-k(a_i-b_i)=b_i(2k-a_i)>=0, connectivity forcing coverage, explicit polynomial encoding and NP certificates. The key estimate is k(r-s)<=T<k; whole-block optimality is never assumed. Classical structural and Set Cover results are credited as established inputs.

Actual primary sources were checked against alternative formulations: Sharifov's induced perfectly matchable objective permits disconnected selections, Weighted Connected Matching maximizes matching-edge weights rather than all induced edges, and constrained-ear and matroid-join results have different objectives. Bounded primary-source, live-register, public Zenodo and local-state checks on 22 October 2026 authenticated no earlier publication of the full target. This is not exhaustive priority, exclusive firstness or current-openness certification. Catalog 30002726 / OWR-13353-012 and project PR1372 identify one result family; source and dependency DOIs are references only.

The deposit consists of the manuscript PDF and a complete editable source and exact-verification ZIP. Standard-library diagnostics compare 10 actual complete-ear/cone/factor-critical objectives, examine 70 set systems / 194 thresholds and 180 full-size forward matching witnesses, test 142 preprocessing cases and 9454 omission identities, and reject 7 false controls. Finite diagnostics supplement the universal proof and do not certify priority. metadata.title: Free spanning-forest degree can decrease under squaring
metadata.description:
The expected root degree of the free uniform spanning forest need not be invariant under squaring an infinite connected locally finite simple vertex-transitive graph. For the binary grandparent graph G, of degree 8, two actual free-exhaustion reductions prove Edeg_FUSF(G)=(24-sqrt(2))/7 > 3.22. For its simple square G^2, of degree 40, a complete finite rational-current certificate on 3070 vertices and 19931 edges proves Edeg_FUSF(G^2) ≤ 3208526010913748780/10^18 < 3.21. All 797240 integer current entries, 122800 divergence equations and 40 energies are checked exactly. Finite Thomson/Rayleigh inequalities followed by free exhaustion justify the infinite free-forest bound; no wired-resistance substitution is made.

With the explicitly adopted convention b_F(X)=Edeg_FUSF(X)/2-1, the strict difference exceeds 1/200. This answers the arbitrary-vertex-transitive assertion in Abért's Some questions (2 November 2010), printed p.4, Question24. That source does not print a normalization formula, so unequal expected degrees and the adopted convention are stated explicitly. The full automorphism group of G is nonunimodular. No negative assertion for the unimodular subclass, another nonunimodular Betti invariant, or the known Cayley case is made.

The grandparent family and Kirchhoff, Thomson, Rayleigh and free-exhaustion methods are established background. Tang's grandparent-forest connectivity and branching work and Pete–Timár's distinct component-count noninvariance are credited. The proposed contribution is the specific expected-degree square comparison, not a new general electrical or forest mechanism. Bounded primary-source investigation authenticated no earlier publication of the complete comparison; no exhaustive novelty, historical firstness or continuing-openness guarantee is asserted. The actual inspected Tang and Pete–Timár bodies are arXiv v2 versions; final journal metadata were authenticated, but the final journal PDFs were inaccessible. The proof and data were already public in project PR1407 before this note; this version is dated 22 October 2026 and is not backdated.

The proposed deposit contains the seven-page paper and a complete source-and-verification ZIP, including the exact current data, an independent standard-library checker, exact outputs, independent finite rational circuit diagnostics, both written infinite derivations, dependencies, priority limits, licenses and offline packaging instructions. No claimant verification program or external solver is trusted for the exact replay. Finite diagnostics do not replace the written universal proofs. metadata.title: A supercritical nonuniqueness example on a graph roughly isometric to the square lattice
metadata.description:
There is an explicit deterministic connected simple graph G of maximum degree four, roughly isometric to the nearest-neighbor square lattice with uniform multiplicative-plus-additive constant 100, for which ordinary common-parameter iid bond percolation satisfies p_c(G)<=9/10 and P_(19/20)(at least two infinite clusters)>2200741829/6461571200>1/3. Every root has positive survival probability already at 9/10. Edges internal to opposite quadrants are retained; every other edge is replaced by a private 100-edge chain. Independent coarse probabilities p and p^100 are an exact series reduction with a bijection of infinite components. An elementary quadrant dual-parity count gives survival at least 143/245, while an all-start/all-length weak-bridge count is strictly below 27/107648.

The five-page note refutes an explicitly declared all-supercritical interpretation of Benjamini's 2013 Problem 9.6: uniqueness for every admissible graph and each fixed p_c(G)<p<=1. The original problem sentence omits its probability quantifier; the preceding chapter discusses the supercritical regime. No uniquely intended missing quantifier is attributed to the author. A weaker near-one uniqueness claim, critical nonuniqueness, almost-sure multiplicity, exact cluster count or simultaneous-in-p law is not asserted. No transitivity, 0/1/infinity law or uniqueness monotonicity is assumed. Bounded subdivision, series reduction, parity and path counting are established methods. Older hyperbolic-sector nonuniqueness, high-density uniqueness, critical product examples and the annealed stretched-lattice series method are credited with their actual model and parameter limits.

Bounded primary-source, native Zenodo, live-register and read-only local-state checks on 22 October 2026 authenticated no earlier full-target publication or solution DOI. This is not exhaustive novelty, exclusive firstness or current-openness certification. The earlier project PR1348 is an unpublished proof source, not an existing published counterexample. Catalog 10000037 / AMR-099-0037 is one result family; source/dependency DOIs are references only.

A new standard-library checker tests 2048 finite corner-containing dual-boundary sets, all 64 bond configurations of a small series replacement with 192 connectivity comparisons and its joint law, a 4392-vertex metric patch with 2116 sampled pairs, 200 explicit weak paths, exact rational constants/tails, and nine false controls. metadata.title: BV generators for polynomial Weyl subalgebras
metadata.description:
For every field k of characteristic zero and every nonzero polynomial h in k[x], the ordinary Hochschild cohomology of A_h = k<x,Y>/(Yx-xY-h(x)), with its canonical cup product and Gerstenhaber bracket, admits a degree-minus-one Batalin-Vilkovisky generator exactly when h is squarefree. The squarefree case has zero bracket and admits Delta=0. If h has a repeated irreducible factor, a central degree-one annihilator forces any bracket generator to vanish on degree one; an explicit cup-zero noncommuting pair then rules out every generator, even without a square-zero requirement. The argument works over the original field without a splitting-field hypothesis. The original embedded h=0 specialization is k[x] and is treated separately.

This gives a classification answering the concrete-family Question (2) in Samuel A. Lopes's contribution, joint work with Andrea Solotar, OWR 46/2023, p.2702. The length-two resolution and derivation structure are established results of Lopes-Solotar and Benkart-Lopes-Ondrus. The older no-generator result and obstruction strategy of Herscovich-Li for FK(3), Documenta Mathematica 27 (2022), Proposition 4.15, DOI 10.4171/DM/X18, are explicitly credited. The note does not claim the first ordinary-Hochschild no-generator phenomenon, exhaustive historical novelty, positive-characteristic generality, or a resolution of the separate general-algebra and Poisson questions. metadata.title: A symmetric ideal chain with periodic Lefschetz behavior in positive characteristic
metadata.description:

metadata.description:

metadata.title: A fixed birational map without a prime-field cycle-distribution limit
metadata.description:
For the fixed birational map L(u,v)=(u,(u²+1)v), every prime p congruent to 3 modulo 4 gives a permutation of the full affine plane F_p². With point-weighted periods normalized by p, the distribution function at every fixed 1/2≤x<1 equals 1−φ(p−1)/(p−1)+o(1), has limsup 1 and liminf at most 23/24. Neither these CDF values nor the period probability measures converge on any further admissible prime subset of positive upper relative density.

A separate proposition covers every odd prime on the invariant regular domain of size p(p-r), where r is zero or two. The primitive principal term is (p-r)φ(p−1)/(p−1). Under uniform-point deletion or arbitrary finite nonnegative assigned periods only on exceptional fibers, bounded statistics change by O(1/p). The regular CDF and a globally bounded continuous ramp thus exclude convergence on every positive-upper-prime-density selection under these conventions. Completed measures are on nonnegative reals; assigned periods may exceed p. Primes congruent to 1 modulo 4 still do not give full-affine permutations.

This is a precisely scoped application to the broad existence assertion in Vivaldi's 2004 Oberwolfach contribution, joint work with Roberts. The triangular family, quadratic primitive-value machinery, shifted-prime totient mean and continuous scalar empirical law are established and credited to the actual sources. The positive-density selection conclusion uses the old atomless scalar law, not merely the existence of two subsequences. No new map family, character-sum theorem, arithmetic mean, scalar law, universal elliptic theorem, polynomial-automorphism theorem or prime-average cycle theorem is claimed.

metadata.title: A continuous free product system not generated by its tensor core
metadata.description:
We construct an associative pointed free product system of separable complex Hilbert spaces whose maximal ordered tensor subsystem does not generate the whole free system. Its tensor core is the time-ordered finite-word Fock system, and the closed free hull of that core is the full finite-word Fock system. The ambient system has additional nonzero orthogonal sectors of ordinal words of length below omega squared. A recoverable sigma-finite Gaussian mixture and coordinate-retaining finite-prefix absorption yield countable maximal-run charts and pointed free-product unitaries. The paper proves full associativity and an explicit continuous-field structure including time zero, positive-time local triviality, and continuity of the structural maps and their inverses. A quantitative finite-positive-measure grade-omega witness proves properness for every positive time.

This gives a negative answer in the scalar specialization to the universal tensor-core generation question posed by Michael Skeide in Oberwolfach Reports 6 (2009), 528-530, DOI10.4171/OWR/2009/09. It does not resolve adapted-cocycle, forward tensor-recovery or general classification questions. The stated explicit continuity convention is part of the theorem; arbitrary stronger regularity axioms are not asserted. Classical Fock constructions, standard Gaussian/Radon-Nikodym tools and nonclassical tensor-noise context are credited. The known forward construction from any spatial tensor input has generating tensor core by a direct hull-monotonicity argument, so it cannot itself give this proper-core-hull obstruction.

metadata.title: A designed tree model with a sharp congestion–fragmentation transition
metadata.description:
We give an analytically tractable designed-tree example motivated by Aldous's conceptual congestion toy-model request. For a bounded-degree binary physical tree with k leaves on each root side and k squared cross-root demand streams, strictly positive linear capacity prices uniquely give the cheapest fixed-topology enlargement carrying doubled unit demands. After design, each stream grows affinely at an independent fixed-law Exp(1) rate. An exact transportation-cut formula and an all-cuts probability estimate confine the joint marginal-admission and spare-connectivity change to an interval of width 16 sqrt(log(k)/k) around mean doubled demand. In the two outer phases every optimizer respectively leaves the whole tree spare or saturates every edge. The window is an upper bound, not an exact critical scaling theorem.

metadata.title: All-load stability of a deterministic-first-chunk file-sharing chain
metadata.description:

metadata.title: Semibrace existence on meet-semilattices: an attributed classification
metadata.description:

metadata.title: Coarse endpoint concentration at every diverging scale for one-dimensional space-time random walks
metadata.description:
For a nearest-neighbor walk on the integers in any fixed independent identically distributed space-time environment whose right-step probabilities lie strictly between zero and one almost surely, we prove superpolynomial concentration of the coarse quenched endpoint law around its averaged law. The intervals may have any deterministic lengths tending to infinity and any deterministic alignments, with no lower growth rate or uniform ellipticity assumption. For every fixed positive discrepancy threshold and every inverse power of time, the corresponding environmental tail is bounded by that inverse power eventually. Constants depend on the fixed law and the eventual threshold may depend on the scale sequence. The theorem gives the affirmative one-dimensional assertion contrary to Conjecture 1 in Noam Berger's contribution to Oberwolfach Report 38/2009.

metadata.title: Explicit Beurling-transform counterexamples in an analytic annihilator
metadata.description:
Both endpoint questions in the bilinear analytic annihilator of Hayman and Lingham, Problem 7.72, have negative answers under the printed negative-kernel convention. The norm-one input v(z)=z/bar(z) on the unit disc annihilates every integrable analytic test function, while its Beurling transform is 1+log|z|^2 and is essentially unbounded. Explicit polynomials v_m(z)=z^2 sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-|z|^2)^j lie in the same annihilator, have norm one and have transform norm H_m, the m-th harmonic number. Each fixed polynomial has bounded transform, but no common uniform constant exists.

This is an exposition and independent explicit verification of consequences of classical formulas, with a self-contained proof. Iwaniec published the exact nonpolynomial witness, output and primitive in 1986. Gill published the general positive-angular transform formula in 2010; the polynomial formula and harmonic-number norm follow by elementary specialization. The 2019 Hayman-Lingham book attributes resolution of Problem 7.72 to Volberg. Its cited reference 52 is the 2008 Banuelos-Janakiraman finite-p paper; the current audit did not locate an explicit full-target account there or a separate Volberg proof. This limitation does not refute the book attribution. No new solution, witness, transform mechanism, first polynomial construction, first harmonic-number calculation or current worldwide openness is claimed. metadata.title: Negative answers to the printed totally mixed face questions
metadata.description:

metadata.title: A negative-curvature normal barrier on an algebraic cone that is not a hyperbolicity cone
metadata.description:

metadata.title: A type-D4 counterexample to the canonical-potential exponent converse
metadata.description:
The exponent-bound converse stated for canonical GHKK potentials in Schumann's 2021 Oberwolfach report is false. For an explicit reduced word in type D4, the canonical potential has 22 combined monomials, all of coefficient one, and all 22 inequalities define distinct facets, although two monomials have exponent minus two in one canonical coordinate. The reduced word and its complete string-coordinate support occur in earlier public computations; we extract the consequence for the historical formulation and supply an independent canonical calculation and exact integer certificates. The chamber-ansatz pullback has all exponents in {-1,0,1}, so the later string-coordinate converse is not refuted. No first-priority or current-openness claim is made.

metadata.title: Vanishing of the cellularization map for non-p-nilpotent component groups
metadata.description:

metadata.title: A credited finiteness deduction for restricted boundary-twist factorizations

metadata.title: An elementary obstruction to same-ground-set matroid-rank approximation
metadata.description:

metadata.title: A classical Wu-manifold answer to a free-rank question

metadata.title: An effective criterion for prescribed block-code extensions
metadata.description:
For a specified onto block self-map f of a nonempty two-sided irreducible sofic shift T, this note gives a complete finite computable criterion for extending that same map into T from a containing shift of finite type. It answers the specified-map question in Boyle's Problem 16.3, including its mixing case. For any total completion F of the local rule, let L be the allowed finite-word language and B the regular two-sided ideal of input words whose finite output is forbidden. Extension is equivalent to locally testable separation of L from B. An irreducibility-based saturation proof converts the credited Place–van Rooijen–Zeitoun2014 Theorem4.2 bound into the single canonical test L(T[N]) intersect B empty, with N=max(2,ell,4(|M|+1)) for a common recognizing monoid M. Success gives F(T[N])=T; failure excludes all other radii, completions and containing alphabets.

Earlier steadiness terminology and Dykstra's2007 broader sofic-homomorphism question, Barth–Dykstra2007 terminology as credited by Ballier, and Ballier's2013/2015 canonical approximation normalization and restricted closing/continuing results are credited. The general LT-separation theorem is published prior machinery, used rather than independently reproved. The result does not solve the separate existence-over-all-maps or cellular-automaton stability questions, or Dykstra's full unrestricted reducible-sofic problem. It claims no new general separation theorem, practical complexity improvement or implemented arbitrary-input solver. Bounded primary-source and citation reviews identified no full predecessor in inspected statements; originality, historical firstness and current worldwide open status remain unestablished. Inaccessible bodies, versions and indexing limits are explicit in the companion archive.

The supporting source archive preserves all48 frozen candidate files, two independent mathematical families, two independent priority reviews and a later peer challenge, exact source hashes and locators, finite automata/symbolic checks and root reproduction receipts. Optimization-safe integrity checks preserve the distinction between example computation and general proof. metadata.title: A missing multiplicity condition for double-permutation sequences
metadata.description:
The four term-sequence axioms printed in the inspected Goodman-Pollack manuscript and the official 2008 Oberwolfach problem session do not imply the proposed connected-set encoding with compatible tangent and separating pseudolines. The explicit two-body period A,B,A,B,C,B,C,B has least period eight, respects both endpoint orders, makes one adjacent different-body swap at each step, and satisfies reverse-toggle half-period symmetry. Every mixed primed/unprimed switch is absent, whereas the required internal tangents must produce mixed events. This is a negative answer to the literal universal realization assertion under those four axioms.

The note also proves that an explicitly required fully separated input term forces every ordered different-body switch exactly once per full period. It does not construct polygons or refute the normalized-input variant. Older stronger allowable-interval definitions are credited to Dhandapani, Goodman, Holmsen and Pollack and to Novick. Habert and Pocchiola already proved the properly constrained specified-fibration representation theorem; the example is outside that input class. No new solution of that stronger theorem is claimed. The source-bound correction concerns the inspected 26 November 2006 author manuscript and official OWR44/2008 passages. The final Goodman-Pollack journal body and an older cited 2004 version were not obtained. Bounded primary-source and citation searches identified no matching earlier literal-negative result, but firstness, exhaustive priority and present-day worldwide open status are not certified.

The companion source archive preserves all 32 frozen candidate files, distinct combinatorial and geometric mathematical audits, two independent priority reviews and exact finite checks. It reproduces the eight-term witness, two independent exhaustive two-body enumerations, separated-start controls, corrupted-input rejection and recursive artifact custody. Software does not formally certify the topological representation theorem, the general proof or literature completeness. metadata.title: Post-Lie nonexistence with a semisimple target
metadata.description: A proof of a unimodular-source obstruction for transverse pairs of homomorphisms into a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra. The perfect nonsemisimple-source post-Lie nonexistence statement follows as a corollary. The argument uses a holomorphic determinant relative invariant and classical Lie-group topology, with explicit attribution of Baues's affine-space predecessor and the earlier post-Lie literature. AI systems were used extensively in solving, checking and writing the work. metadata.title: A flag-curve proof of an original-side pedal-area invariant
metadata.description: For a noncircular ellipse and a proper nested confocal elliptical caustic whose primitive least billiard period is divisible by four, the signed original trajectory area times the signed area of its original-side-line pedal polygon is independent of phase for every fixed finite real point M. This attributed research note presents a complete incidence-curve proof: disjoint possible simple pole supports and complementary reversal zeros make the product holomorphic on a compact genus-one flag curve. Primitive stars, both orientations and zero or negative pedal areas are included. The exact theorem, N4 formula and a rescaled signed star example also occur in Alper Ferudun's contemporary Pedal Areas of Periodic Elliptic Billiard Trajectories with Respect to an Arbitrary Point, version1.0 DOI10.5281/zenodo.23400541, prominently credited. Steiner's pedal-area principle, the Bialy-Tabachnikov four-period implication and established Schwartz-Tabachnikov, Akopyan-Schwartz-Tabachnikov and Chavez-Caliz flag/meromorphic methods are prior mathematics. No theorem or method novelty, first disclosure or certified independent discovery is claimed. The currently public PR203 record reports October1 creation and the exact contemporary Zenodo deposit October15 creation; these separate object dates do not certify historical visibility, discovery time or independence. The source table does not literally print least period; an exact doubled-six nominal-twelve counterexample protects that qualification. LaTeX source and verification materials include all18 preserved original submission files, independent derivations, explicit-exception portable checks, finite noninterval physical diagnostics and bounded source/priority ledgers. metadata.title: The outer center-pedal area product in elliptic billiards
metadata.description: For periodic billiards between strictly nested nondegenerate confocal ellipses, the product of the signed areas of the outer tangent polygon and the perpendicular projection of the ellipse center onto its side lines is constant when the period is not divisible by four. The note proves the original k303,b assertion of Reznik-Garcia-Koiller (2020 arXiv;2021 published edition), including admissible coprime stars and fixed repeated traversals, and provides an explicit invariant value. The actual center-foot map is a fixed linear image of a phase-shifted edge-vector polygon. Classical KLS2002 cyclic Jacobi, KS2003/2004 Landen, AST/BT2020 foot-velocity and hodograph, Stachel canonical coordinates, conic polarity and established meromorphic methods are credited. A. Ferudun2026 version1.1, DOI10.5281/zenodo.23088516, Theorem2/Section6, gives the exact complete contemporary theorem. Historical ordering, independent non-derivation and novelty remain undetermined; no first-proof, exclusive-resolution, new-identity or current-worldwide-open claim is made. metadata.title: A flag-curve proof of an outer-pedal area invariant
metadata.description: For a noncircular ellipse and a proper nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic with primitive least period N congruent to two modulo four, the signed area of the outer tangent polygon times its signed arbitrary-point pedal area is phase independent. The note presents an alternative flag-curve proof on the genus-one quotient: the original and pedal area traces have the same two possible simple poles; Riemann-Roch and reversal force proportionality. A self-contained verification of the credited Chavez-Caliz original/outer area product in this parity completes the proof. Primitive stars, reversal and signed zero or negative pedal areas are included. Alper Ferudun's contemporary Outer-Pedal Area Products in Elliptic Billiards, version1.0 DOI10.5281/zenodo.23087221 and version1.1 DOI10.5281/zenodo.23088516, already states the exact theorem, general six-period formula and repeated-triangle qualification, and is prominently credited. metadata.title: An explicit rank-two entropy-minimizing Fano degeneration
metadata.description:
We give an explicit smooth Fano fivefold whose unique global Han–Li entropy-minimizing valuation has rational rank two and is therefore nondivisorial. Its canonical first central variety is singular, so this first degeneration is nontrivial. The example is the product of Miao–Wang's established quadric-blowup threefold with the first Hirzebruch surface. Exact moment equations specify the two positive weights. A universal resultant argument and the classical Hermite–Lindemann theorem prove that their ratio is irrational. The associated graded anticanonical ring, canonical weight normalization, weak product soliton equation, and application of the established global optimality criterion are made explicit.

The construction satisfies the request discussed by Blum in Oberwolfach Report 17/2022, pp. 888–889, without a dimension bound or a product exclusion. Major inputs are due to Miao–Wang, Wang–Zhu, Han–Li, and Blum–Liu–Xu–Zhuang. Earlier nontrivial first centers of Li–Li are credited; their second example's rational rank was not certified in the sources inspected. The threefold factor was already announced in Miao–Wang's January 2024 preprint. No novelty, historical firstness, exhaustive priority, or continued-openness certificate is claimed.

AI tools were used extensively in developing, checking, and preparing the work. The reported adversarial reviews were performed by AI agents. This is an unrefereed preprint; independent human peer review and formal verification have not been completed. The accompanying verification archive preserves original proof and correction bytes, source fingerprints, bounded priority audits, adversarial analyses, and exact auxiliary diagnostics. Passing software checks does not formally verify the geometric or analytic theorem inputs.

metadata.title: Pure point Dirichlet spectrum on quasi-conical domains
metadata.description:
For every integer dimension at least two, this note constructs some connected open quasi-conical tower whose form-defined Dirichlet Laplacian has a complete orthonormal eigenbasis, spectrum and essential spectrum equal to the nonnegative half-line, dense positive eigenvalues, no zero eigenfunction, and no absolutely or singular continuous spectral subspace. Both expanding cube widths and positive shrinking windows are chosen inductively. The windows are openings in zero-thickness interface screens. No arbitrary preassigned-width, smooth-boundary, Neumann, positive-length passage or effective numerical aperture theorem is asserted.

The result answers the precise existential spectral-type question in Krejcirik and Lotoreichik, Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 56 (2024), Sections 2.2, 3 and 5, and the corresponding Oberwolfach contribution (OWR-14297736-021). Their geometry, freedom of future cube sizes and finite-window convergence are substantive antecedents. Whole spectral families and multiplicity control are credited to Hempel, Seco and Simon (1991), Proposition 1.4, and the warning in KL Remark 3.1. The additional construction exhaustively transports complete finite spectral clusters with summable norm errors. Repeated dense probes prove basis completeness. No new abstract finite-rank diagonalization principle is claimed. Bounded primary-source, author/citation and direct Zenodo searches located no full matching predecessor; historical first priority and current worldwide openness are not certified. Some older full bodies, a restricted finite-dimensional gap-note body, and unindexed or nonpublic work remain outside the comparison.

The companion source archive preserves all 39 frozen candidate files, distinct geometric and spectral audits, an explicitly superseding source-reading correction, priority searches and a fresh priority challenge. Offline checks reproduce integrity and finite diagnostics; they do not formally certify the PDE theorem or exhaustive priority. metadata.title: Global Hessian realizations of statistical manifolds
metadata.description:
Every smooth Hausdorff second-countable statistical manifold of fixed finite dimension n at least 1, without boundary and with positive-definite metric, admits a proper global statistical embedding into an open subset of R^N with one smooth positive Hessian potential, where N=binomial(2n+4,3). Orthogonal projection of the standard flat connection and its metric dual induces the prescribed ordered pair of torsion-free dual connections. For a general mutually dual pair, both torsions vanishing is necessary and sufficient for realization by a torsion-free dually flat ambient manifold. Countable zero-dimensional inputs are treated separately. The ambient neighborhood may be nonconvex and incomplete; dual affine coordinates are local. No finite-probability-model, global-gradient-injectivity or optimal-dimension conclusion is asserted.

The construction answers the historical realization question in item1(a) of Furuhata, Matsuzoe and Urakawa, Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics (1998), in the stated smooth positive boundaryless scope. A proper Whitney embedding followed by all polynomial features through degree three gives a fixed finite scalar-jet spanning family. A smooth fiberwise right inverse produces an exact global Lauritzen pair, including the prescribed cubic and connection signs. A normal-neighborhood extension and a nonuniform Schur-complement penalty give one positive Hessian potential on a neighborhood of the entire embedded manifold, without compactness or uniform geometric bounds.

This is a fully credited self-contained construction note. Lauritzen, Matumoto, Le, the Nash/Gromov free-map lineage, Marugame, Whitney and tubular-neighborhood theory provide substantial ancestry; Osipov gives genuine global special-curvature predecessors. Early unrestricted finite-simplex claims are disclosed. Actual Ay-Jost-Le-Schwachhofer2017 Theorems4.10 and4.11 distinguish finite models for compact inputs from countable models for noncompact inputs. Bounded independent primary-source priority audits did not establish a verified unrestricted predecessor, but material final-body access gaps remain. Historical novelty, first priority and continued openness of the question are not certified.

The deposit includes the editable LaTeX source and an explicit-inventory verification package preserving all33 original PR946 files byte for byte, curated mathematical and priority reviews, exact symbolic controls and separately bounded numerical replay. The original strict platform-dependent floating-output mismatch is preserved; current transport compares twelve named finite sample floats under documented tolerances and every other mathematical field exactly. Those tolerances are diagnostics, not proved roundoff bounds, and finite controls do not replace the universal proof. The original PR declares4/5 proof responses, but native historical invocation events were unavailable; the audit adds zero proof-search responses and fabricates no history. Raw third-party source bodies are excluded. AI tools were used extensively in research, proof development, source checking, computation, writing and adversarial review. This preprint is unrefereed; no independent human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification is claimed.

metadata.title: The least-period criterion for outer focal products in elliptic billiards
metadata.description: For a noncircular ellipse and a fixed proper nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic with primitive least billiard period N at least three, the ordinary product of distances from consecutive boundary-tangent intersections to either original focus is phase independent if and only if four divides N. All admissible coprime star windings are covered; the two constants then agree. A paired-distance factorization and cyclic divisor prove both directions, with an explicit odd-period argument and the exceptional four-period degree drop. Repeated traversals cannot restore constancy. The positive direction is the primitive interpretation of k115 and is also proved by Alper Ferudun, Focal Distance Products of Outer Elliptic Billiard Polygons, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23093258; its closely overlapping mechanism and explicit constant are prominently credited. Canonical billiard parametrization, polarity and elliptic-function norm methods are established background. The observed October 1 GitHub PR and October 2 competing deposit/DOI registration document contemporaneous separate treatments, not certified first disclosure or independent discovery. The converse was added during the October 16 audit; its historical novelty is unestablished. The deposit contains the six-page research note, LaTeX source and portable verification package with exact reflection/tangency certificates, divisor checks, direct tangent-intersection controls and bounded priority/source ledgers. metadata.title: Near-one oriented-percolation flow from Bernoulli first-passage estimates
metadata.description:
For the canonical square-lattice oriented Bernoulli edge-capacity flow, the note derives 1-v(p)~sqrt(2(1-p)) as p increases to one, the asymptotic posed by Aldous and Lenderman in 2004. The sources are the left and bottom boundaries excluding the top-left and bottom-right sink corners; the sinks are the top and right boundaries. Shared vertices are allowed among edge-disjoint paths. The exact finite directed-cut identity, its bounded boundary terms, and the fixed-parameter volume limit followed by the small-defect limit are supplied. The source-stated deterministic L1 flow-density limit is an explicit input; the expectation limit also follows from diagonal superadditivity.

The entire asymptotic is presented as an explicitly attributed corollary of Basdevant-Gouere-Theret's public 2021 strict-site score scaling and weighted-list computation in arXiv:2106.12266v1, Section 3.3, equation (33), with its m=0 numerical terms. A precise model-event inclusion groups outgoing rare-edge marks into independent site marks of probability 2q-q^2. The ordinary undirected first-passage theorem alone is not substituted for the asymmetric cut model with zero-cost backward traversals. This is an application identifying an older-estimate consequence, not a new central rare-defect, Poisson, BK or detour estimate. No novelty, historical-firstness, exhaustive-priority or present-day-openness claim is made. An earlier explicit statement of this particular flow corollary was not located in bounded searches; its first recognition remains unestablished. Exact equation references were checked in the public 2021 v1, not in a retrieved final journal body.

The deposit contains the research note and a verification archive with editable source, all thirty immutable original files and their proof/audit history, the longer BK-Poisson argument, independent mathematical and bounded priority assessments, finite falsification controls, source fingerprints, closed typed inventories, an isolated archival replay launcher and a deterministic ZIP builder. The current launcher distinguishes historical requested flags from measured isolated execution flags. Optional source-only authentication checks all three complete native corpora and four exact primary bodies without executing archival code; those third-party bodies and raw corpora are excluded from the deposit. Finite checks and cryptographic hashes supplement the analytic proof and do not prove the asymptotic or novelty. Compressed-byte reproducibility requires identical inputs and the same Python ZIP implementation and zlib runtime.

The claim concerns the prescribed edge-capacity model, not vertex-disjoint flow, other boundary conventions or other graph families. Classical Poisson-chain and product-BK inputs, and Verges's 2025 overlapping-region decomposition/skeleton work, are credited for the preserved alternative proof. AI tools were used extensively in mathematical development, source review, writing, computation and adversarial checking. The recorded adversarial reviews were performed by AI agents. metadata.title: A vertex maximum principle for subcritical reinforcement
metadata.description:
A self-contained alternative proof of unique strictly positive equilibrium and simultaneous almost-sure coordinatewise homogenization for subcritical graph-based reinforcement. The graph is countable, undirected and simple, with bounded degree; vertex firing rates are positive and bounded above, but their infimum may be zero. The exponent satisfies 0 <= alpha < 1. Initial edge counts are arbitrary finite deterministic positive integers. The proof uses finite-volume vertex minimization, an exact compensated jump transform, and a maximum principle for bounded positive complete vertex trajectories. Unrestricted nonnegative-equilibrium uniqueness is false; the positive statement is an explicitly corrected formulation.

Shuo Qin, arXiv:2610.11780v1, Theorem 1.1 (submitted 8 October 2026), supplies the full positive theorem and broader real initialization. It is prominently credited, together with the matching example in Remark 1.3, the older finite-WARM matching mechanism, and the 2018/2021 partial results of Couzinie and Hirsch. The vertex proof here is different, while the power/incidence and complete-limit strategy are shared structural ideas. Angel-Hermon-Yao work reported by Qin was not available as a verified full manuscript with a public date. Repository PR764 has a server creation date of 5 October 2026, but this does not certify the first public availability of current proof bytes. No first, sole, new-theorem or currently-open claim is made. metadata.title: The outer focal-pedal area product in odd elliptic billiards
metadata.description: For a fixed odd least-period billiard family between strictly nested nondegenerate confocal ellipses, project the two original foci onto the ordered side lines of the outer tangent polygon. The complete proof uses the explicit focal-foot map, paired collinear residues, reduced real period and complementary zeros on a compact torus. Classical auxiliary-circle geometry, Stachel canonical coordinates, Jacobi and cyclic elliptic identities, older Poncelet-area methods and Khare-Sukhatme2004 generalized Landen identity are explicitly credited. The archive provides a complete alternative geometric reduction to that old identity and a pole-space comparison to Ferudun2026 original focal-inversion areas; those additional geometric applications are distinguished from literal earlier printed target proofs. metadata.title: An interior second-order defect from a Hele-Shaw contact arc
metadata.description: A detailed attributed proof/application of Ross–Witt Nyström's smooth Hele-Shaw contact-arc construction. The associated bounded weak homogeneous complex Monge–Ampère solution on P1 times the disc lacks a second-order real Taylor expansion at a genuine interior point, despite smooth strictly positive fibre boundary forms. A zero-area arc filling gives a strict Green-function time-slope gap; finite negative curvature on the smooth covering-space family and global concavity give incompatible Legendre quadratic coefficients. The contact geometry, strong flow, obstacle identity and duality are prior. metadata.title: A periodic counterexample to the diffuse allocation characterization
metadata.description:
An explicit periodic diffuse measure on R^2 has a rooted law invariant under every measurable, pointwise-covariant, measure-preserving allocation determined by its original observed state, but fails the full joint mass-stationarity identity. The measure consists of horizontal Lebesgue lines with alternating densities one and two. Covariance and a finite per-period mass equation cover all allocations, including noninjective maps. In the defining unit-square mass-resampling experiment, the heavy-root event has probability two thirds instead of zero. A constant accompanying random element suffices. This gives a negative answer to Thorisson's historical Problem 4.1 and Last-Thorisson's Problem 7.5 in their stated unrestricted scope.

The entire existential negative conclusion is an elementary consequence of Last-Thorisson (2009), Example 7.1, their Lebesgue-product mass-stationarity proposition already in arXiv:1405.7566v1 (2014), Section 8 Proposition 1, retained in the 2015 version, and the full allocation-transfer calculation displayed in the note. Last-Thorisson (2023), Section 8 and Remark 8.1, give the canonical diffuse parallel-line/invariant-direction balancing obstruction; Khezeli-Mellick (2025), final Remark 3.2, explicitly identifies the product/atomic-quotient balancing-allocation reduction. Those balancing-existence statements have a distinct scope from the self-preserving characterization. The periodic rational-weight model is an elementary worked illustration of these established mechanisms. No new-discovery, novelty, firstness, exhaustive-priority or worldwide-current-openness claim is made. The first explicit recognition of the combined corollary and priority of the exact periodic formula remain unestablished by bounded searches.

The example is singular, two-dimensional and has a continuous translation stabilizer. It supplies no counterexample for positive-density measures, one-dimensional diffuse measures, free actions, absence of invariant directions, independent stationary backgrounds, or invariance under all preserving Markov kernels. An explicit preserving Markov kernel changes its rooted type. The exact pointwise-covariance convention is essential; an unspecified spatial-almost-everywhere representative with an unrestricted root value is a different formulation.

metadata.title: An odd-period product for focal inversions of outer billiard polygons
metadata.description: For a fixed odd least-period elliptic billiard family with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, we prove constancy of the product of the signed straight-edge areas obtained by unit inversion of the outer tangent-polygon vertices about the two original billiard foci. metadata.title: Deep derived pure braids need not be 1-solvable
metadata.description:
For every m at least 3 and every finite positive integer k, the kth ordinary derived subgroup of the classical disk pure braid group P_m contains a braid whose standard oriented closure is not integrally smoothly 1-solvable. Consequently P_m^(n+2) is not contained in F_n^m for every integer n at least 1. This answers negatively Question 3 of Shelly Harvey's contribution, joint work with JungHwan Park and Arunima Ray, Pure braids, Whitney towers, and 0-solvability, Oberwolfach Reports50/2017, printed3021/MFO PDF35, published2018. The witness may depend on the finite depth; no common braid in the intersection of all derived terms is asserted. P1 and P2 have trivial positive derived subgroups.

The proof combines the established Gambaudo-Ghys ordinary closure-signature quasimorphism, its explicitly nonhomomorphic restriction to P3, and persistence through solvable derived quotients. Nonzero homogeneous signature is converted to nonzero ordinary signature by taking a power. The universal pointwise signature obstruction is proved from Otto's actual integral smooth solution definition using the signed cellular rank bound, integral universal coefficients, twisted surface classes, unit dual intersections and rank saturation, followed by Toffoli's surgery formula at -1 without an Alexander-root exclusion. The general quasimorphism facts are prior results: Calegari gives amenable rigidity, and Kawasaki-Kimura-Maruyama-Matsushita-Mimura2025Lemma7.12 proves a stronger defect-restriction identity. No new general group theorem is claimed. Bounded independent primary priority searches through October15,2026 did not establish an earlier complete answer to this precise braid-solvability question; no first-priority or continued-openness certification follows.

The four-page unrefereed research note is accompanied by identical editable LaTeX/PDF, all44 unchanged original PR938 files, eight curated independent mathematical/source/reproducibility/priority/mechanism audit families, source-access records, and a closed-inventory standard-library POSIX release verifier. The original explicit104-letter braid in P3^(3) has closure signature -2, certified independently by a48-dimensional planar Goeritz form of inertia(23,25,0) and a104-term Burau-Meyer calculation. That finite witness proves n=1 only and is separate from the all-depth existential argument. Current replay requires Python3.10+ and os.O_NOFOLLOW; it authenticates copied bytes and compares complete exact saved mathematical outputs under an isolated nonoptimized worker. metadata.title: Quantitative persistence in a fixed-city area equation
metadata.description:
For every fixed finite collection of at least two distinct interior sites in the unit square and every strictly positive initial probability vector, consider the hard weighted-Voronoi area equation z_i prime = A_i(z) - z_i, where city i maximizes z_i^alpha times distance to the power -beta. We give a quantitative all-coordinate persistence theorem when beta > 2 alpha: an explicit time-dependent lower bound, a positive bound for all time, and a positive limiting inferior bound independent of the starting state. An asymmetric three-city instance with alpha=2, beta=8 has every share between 1/4096 and 2047/2048 for all nonnegative time. This refutes the unrestricted alpha > 1 collapse alternative in the literal 2007 Conjecture 32(a) and the catalog conjunction containing it. The result does not establish convergence, equilibrium uniqueness, initial-value independence of a limit, or stochastic city-founding conclusions. Zero initial weights, coincident sites, boundary sites, and the one-city case are outside the stated theorem.

The model and conjecture are Aldous's. Multiplicatively weighted Voronoi/Apollonius geometry is classical; the original 2007 notes already contain the protected-neighborhood mechanism and area exponent 2 alpha / beta in an unfinished stochastic argument. The scalar substitution and integrating-factor step are standard. Ferudun's unrefereed preprint, stated release 14 October 2026, explicitly gives robust two-city Conjecture 32(a) counterexamples in another parameter range and records the ratio-invariance inconsistency. Its proved every-exponent derivative lemma and position continuity also imply qualitative two-city noncollapse in the present beta > 2 alpha regime. These overlapping conclusions receive direct credit. The present theorem supplies all-site, all-positive-initial-state quantitative persistence; it is not advertised as the first negative answer or as a new geometric method. The original complete PR was recorded on 6 October 2026, but chronology and bounded searches certify neither firstness, exhaustive novelty nor worldwide current openness.

metadata.title: Off-interval spectral convergence for geometrically consistent discrete dipoles
metadata.description: We give an independent proof of the off-interval eigenvalue approximation described in Costabel's OWR43/2022 discrete-dipole question, under an explicit geometric condition: center-selected cubic voxel unions converge in volume to the bounded measurable particle. This includes every bounded Lipschitz particle, for arbitrary grid translations. At every fixed complex frequency, the actual zero-diagonal matrices have no spectral pollution outside the exact static lattice interval, uniform resolvent stability there, and approximation of isolated eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity, norm-convergent embedded Riesz projections and generalized spectral subspaces. The proof combines Costabel--Dauge--Nedaiasl's established static lattice interval with strong static consistency, Hilbert--Schmidt convergence of the actual sampled dynamic correction and classical compact spectral approximation. A separate compact positive-volume empty-interior support has a nonreal continuum pole at frequency1/10000 while every matrix on the rational meshes is 3x3 zero; its support index is existential. metadata.title: Property (T) above one-third density in random free-product quotients
metadata.description:
Fix at least three nontrivial finitely generated groups, a finite nonempty inverse-closed generating alphabet of nonidentity elements in each factor, and a density 1/3 less than d less than 1. For the quotient by floor(|S_l|^d) independent uniform rooted cyclically reduced syllable relators of exact length l, sampled with replacement, the probability of Kazhdan property (T) tends to one through all integer lengths. This gives an affirmative resolution of the at-least-three-factor property-(T) question in Problem 16 of the 2026 Oberwolfach report Median Geometry and Applications. Fixed-radius word-ball alphabets with integer radius at least one are included. The theorem does not settle the broader two-factor Question 1.9 of Random Quotients of Free Products, the critical density 1/3, or varying-parameter uniformity. Known collapse already gives property (T) above 1/2; the substantive extension includes every density in (1/3,1/2].

The proof completes model-specific steps of an established spectral program. Montee and Steenbock already proposed the syllable-respecting three-part strategy in their project report in ESI Annual Report 2024, pp.77-79, especially p.78; that volume is copyright 2025 with an August 2025 preface. Ashcroft already treats all integer lengths with almost-equal blocks in the ordinary free-group model, and Drutu-Mackay supply the common-suffix finite-index precedent. The present argument supplies the exact weighted endpoint kernel, torsion-compatible inverse-fixed-block deletion and suffix choices, unequal-length type-matrix spectrum, and concentration of independent whole-relator Laplacians. It uses established Ballmann-Swiatkowski-Zuk/Kotowski-Kotowski and Tropp results. No invention of the general strategy, new spectral criterion, verified firstness, exhaustive novelty, or worldwide current-open-status certificate is claimed.

metadata.title: Counterexamples to Satoh's SL(2) representation-filtration conjecture
metadata.description: We give explicit counterexamples to the equality of the integral Andreadakis filtration A_n(k) and the SL(2,C) representation filtration D_n(k) formulated in Satoh's 2018 Oberwolfach report. The proof uses a classical degree-five Lie identity, explicitly credited to Burde arXiv:1411.0950v2 equation(4) and Theorem4.14, with its Razmyslov attribution reported through that inspected source; the degree-six identity is a weighted substitution. metadata.title: Finite-energy lattice percolation with internal critical probability one
metadata.description:
For every integer d at least 2, we construct a nearest-neighbor bond percolation on the integer lattice Z^d whose law is invariant under every graph automorphism and mixing under translations. It has ordinary finite energy: both single-edge conditional states have strictly positive probability given all the other output edges. Almost surely there is a unique infinite component C, but the quenched internal Bernoulli bond and site critical probabilities of X and C equal one. Every independent thinning with retention p below one destroys all infinite components. This gives an affirmative construction for the historical ordinary-energy question of Benjamini, Haggstrom and Schramm, restated in Benjamini's Saint-Flour notes and by Benjamini and Tassion.

The construction develops Haggstrom-Mester's published one-ended-tree summable-flip mechanism. Tree edges are deleted with probability 2^(-s), where s is their finite-side size; a non-tree edge is inserted with probability 2^(-M), where M is the maximum finite-side size along its connecting tree path. This dimension independent rule suppresses every bypass and leaves eventually singleton cut boundaries along each ray. Timar's established equivariant one-ended spanning-tree theorem supplies the all-dimensional input. The note also proves a planar bounded-cutset consequence of the exact fixed-phase midpoint projection of the older Haggstrom-Mester site model, whose unchanged flip rates are 4^(-s). That consequence is a deduction supplied here, not a theorem located in the inspected older paper. metadata.title: Intermediate-area cylinders in the principal quadratic stratum
metadata.description: We derive a Poisson limit for intermediate cylinder areas in the principal holomorphic quadratic stratum Q(1^(4g-4)), with the square-count cutoff tending to infinity before the genus. metadata.title: Forward generation does not ensure GNS descent: an explicit continuous counterexample
metadata.description: Generation by an observed algebra and its forward translates does not ensure descent through a general dilation's fixed expectation-GNS representation. metadata.title: Failure of strong quadratic growth in unregularized sparse control of a critical wave equation
metadata.description: We give an explicit negative answer to retaining ordinary critical-cone strict positivity and strong control-L2 quadratic growth after removing quadratic control regularization from the Kunisch–Meinlschmidt energy-critical quintic-wave model. Local L1 quadratic growth survives, with fixed-basepoint weaker-norm bounds. Every fixed finite nonnegative terminal-velocity weight is allowed; the radial lower comparison neighborhood may depend on that weight. metadata.title: Generic Cantor actions of Z wr Z are hyperfinite
metadata.description:

metadata.title: A smooth Reshetnyak-harmonic sphere with unbounded distortion
metadata.description:

metadata.title: An application of separable-state nonrepresentability to Grassmann orbitopes and calibrations

metadata.description:

metadata.title: A Robinson counterexample to ideal-only tangency certificates
metadata.description:

The standard sphere-minimization mechanism retains its attribution to Laurent's updated manuscript dated 6 February 2010, Section 7.2.3, Lemma 7.21, manuscript pages 117-118 (https://homepages.cwi.nl/~monique/files/moment-ima-update-new.pdf). The earlier 2009 published chapter has a different Lemma 7.21; its DOI is bibliographic context, not the tangency locator. Robinson's form and classical zero-set ingredients retain their attribution. metadata.title: A Martin kernel with isolated Harnack contact in an annulus
metadata.description:

metadata.title: Local Ricci-pinching maxima on an almost-abelian group
metadata.description:

The proof covers the full space of nearby metrics through an orthogonal slice with an unrestricted cross-block and a uniform remainder estimate along a constant-value family. metadata.title: Full stress stratifications determine a labelled graph
metadata.description:
For every positive n and d, a simple graph on a fixed labelled vertex set is determined by its full connected coordinate-sign self-stress partition of (R^d)^n, with all vertex collisions retained. An unordered pair is an edge exactly when its collision diagonal is a union of whole strata. Thus two such partitions are literally equal precisely when their edge sets agree. This gives a complete answer to the literal equality interpretation of Problem 4 in Karpenkov (2018), DOI 10.1007/s40598-018-0080-7.

The proof combines Panina's known collapsed-edge criterion with elementary positive diagonal transport along a connected collinear path. No novelty is claimed for the detector, stress equivalence machinery, collinear invariance or incidence normalization. The note exhibits nonisomorphic trees with ambient-linearly equivalent full stratifications.

metadata.title: Positive tangent-bundle Seshadri constants characterize projective space
metadata.description:
Let X be a smooth integral projective variety of dimension n at least one over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic. Positivity of the relative Fulger-Murayama Seshadri constant of the tangent bundle at one arbitrary closed point implies that X is projective n-space. The five-page research note proves Fulger-Murayama Conjecture 4.9 without assuming Fano, global tangent nefness, characteristic zero, or a general point.

An absolute minimum of ample degree through the specified point eliminates the boundary of the one-marked stable-map family. Very-free evaluation and the actual contracted marking section give numerical Picard rank one and ampleness of the anticanonical divisor; the established Fano clause completes the proof. Standard numerical-generation methods, Mori/Kollar, Fulger-Murayama, and Chang's toric case are credited. metadata.title: The outer-pedal area centroid in even-period elliptic billiards
metadata.description: We prove the k307 outer-side pedal area-centroid observation of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller for billiards in a noncircular ellipse with a strict confocal elliptic caustic and least even period. The ordered perpendicular feet of any fixed point on the boundary tangent lines have an explicit phase-independent signed area centroid wherever their signed area is nonzero. We classify the entire zero-area locus: none when d is nonnegative, and a fixed circle when d is negative. Simple winding-one even families have a centroid for every fixed point; the four-period value is M/3. An exact primitive eight-period star shows that the exceptional undefined locus is real. The note supplies an all-period support-coordinate and cubic-moment proof. metadata.title: An elementary counterexample to a Nullstellensatz for finite-type link invariants
metadata.description:
We give a principal-ideal counterexample to the arbitrary-ideal actual-link Nullstellensatz in the ordinary uncompleted complex algebra of all finite-order finite-type link invariants. With g the sum of squared pairwise linking numbers and f=g(4g-1), the nonempty common zero set is the algebraically split links, but g does not lie in the radical of fV. A character on the entire algebra is obtained by formal evaluation of the standard twist-restriction polynomial at one half. The result applies for every fixed component count m at least two and for all finite-component links; the source's separate indexed linking-number ideal in the labelled theory is not decided.

metadata.title: NP-completeness of three-terminal shortest-path blocking
metadata.description:
We prove NP-completeness of undirected, unit-traversal-length three-terminal Blocking Shortest Paths: delete a minimum edge set to increase every pairwise terminal distance by at least one. Hardness holds with unit deletion costs and all three original terminal distances equal to three. A direct Vertex Cover reduction also proves NP-completeness when all terminal distances must remain finite, or increase exactly from three to four. The result classifies the undirected triangle question posed by Stefan Krause in 2005. The classical subdivision identity is credited to Poljak (1974), and the related tripartite attachment mechanism to Khachiyan and coauthors (2008). metadata.title: Loss of total-space positivity for the normalized relative Kähler–Ricci flow
metadata.description:

metadata.description:

metadata.title: A regular zero-area singularity with a nonzero weak Bianchi defect
metadata.description:

The spacetime is a negative-mass specialization of the known Dadhich-Kar-Mukherjee-Visser metric, whose tensor formulas are credited. Its static slices have harmonically regular zero-area singularities of mass -2a. We prove absolute convergence of the complete weak Bianchi scalar for every permitted test and compute an explicit nonzero boundary functional, with value -8 pi for a normalized radial test. metadata.title: No single polynomial inequality defines a real binary Gram locus
metadata.description:
For a real tensor with n binary factors, the Gram locus is the tuple of determinants of its one-mode Gram matrices as the tensor ranges over the closed Frobenius unit ball. For every n>=3, no single real polynomial nonnegativity condition in those determinant coordinates defines this locus inside the cube [0,1/4]^n, or inside its known convex hull. This gives a negative answer to Seigal's single-polynomial question for n>=4. The self-contained proof uses established marginal polygon inequalities, an explicit real three-factor realization, exact polynomial multiplicities and zero-determinant slices. A strictly positive rational four-factor tuple also passes the proposed polynomial condition but is unrealizable at any allowed norm.

metadata.title: A counterexample to ideal closure of property-(s) elements in skew braces
metadata.description:

metadata.title: Missing faces and topological embeddings of sphere skeleta
metadata.description:

metadata.title: Nonunique nearest stable complex quadratics
metadata.description:

The monic quadratic abscissa nevertheless is function prox-regular at the origin relative to each finite limiting subgradient, with constants depending on that subgradient in the real Euclidean coefficient metric.

This gives a negative answer in degree two to Lewis's historical question about the stable complex monic set. The later Oberwolfach Question1 omits the coefficient field, normalization and metric; its complex convention is explicitly qualified. The note credits Bottema and Kirillov-Overton classical stability-boundary geometry, Burke-Overton/Lewis first-order root analysis, the Poliquin-Rockafellar-Thibault projection characterization, and earlier nearest-polynomial approximation work of Moses-Liu and Orban de Xivry. metadata.title: An exact period criterion for focal-distance products in elliptic billiards

metadata.title: An exact six-period correction to the printed elliptic billiard assertion k108
metadata.description:

The horizontal coordinates and caustic are explicitly credited to Garcia–Reznik, arXiv:2011.06640v1, Appendix B.5.1 (12 November 2020), and its 2022 published successor. metadata.title: A four-period counterexample to the conjectured elliptic billiard invariant k107
metadata.description:

A self-contained continuous-family proof checks physical reflection, strict caustic contact interiors and all denominators.

The general four-periodic construction, its caustic and area identities are credited to Garcia and Reznik. metadata.title: An explicit joint Laplace transform for Brownian first-visit cell lengths on a circle
metadata.description:

For arbitrary fixed distinct labeled seeds, equally spaced seeds, and independent uniform seeds, the full joint Laplace transform is an absolutely convergent series with coefficients reduced to finite permutation sums and deterministic integrals of explicit interval-exit kernels over cumulative physical-clock inequalities. A uniform factorial bound controls the outer series, and compact-support moment determinacy fixes the joint measure. metadata.title: The vertex centroid of focal antipedals of even elliptic billiards
metadata.description:
We prove invariant k405 for the original-polygon, full-line antipedals of elliptic billiards with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic and even least period. The unweighted vertex centroid is zero for the center pole and has an explicit phase-independent focal coefficient determined by the axes, caustic parameter, period and perimeter. The proof covers primitive star polygons and either orientation; the circle is treated separately. Repeated odd polygons with even list length and hyperbolic or degenerate caustics are outside the theorem. A self-contained finite-action and perimeter-stationarity proof and portable exact verification supplement are supplied.

This answers k405 as posed without proof in Reznik-Garcia-Koiller's 2020/2021 source. Ferudun's later deposited note, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23092466, states the same theorem and coefficient and uses the same pair-and-moment mechanism; that overlap is explicitly credited. A proof was publicly posted in PR140 on September 30, 2026, before the specific overlapping Zenodo record was created on October 1. metadata.title: Ordinary Banach–Mazur rigidity of von Neumann algebras
metadata.description: For every fixed complex von Neumann algebra M, an algebra-dependent positive ordinary complex Banach–Mazur threshold ensures that every von Neumann algebra N within that threshold is Jordan *-isomorphic to M. Roydor announced the general conditional implication in 2020, while his published Theorem 1.2 assumes separable predual. The note gives an explicit proof extension using deformation stability on two fixed source algebras and reconstruction of odd finite type-I summands from full abelian projections. metadata.title: Rational-point undecidability for smooth projective varieties over the rational numbers

metadata.title: Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization
metadata.description: We give a deterministic reduction for complete sparse univariate polynomial factorization over explicitly represented finite fields.
