metadata.title: Metric rigidity at the boundary of cubic compactifications
metadata.description: This note deduces a sharp Cartier-index criterion for irreducible normal projective complex klt Fano varieties of positive dimension carrying a weak Kahler–Einstein metric with bounded potentials: an ample Cartier root -K_X = rL with r > dim(X)/2 + 1 forces stable tangent sheaves on finite quasi-etale covers and rigidity of parallel orthogonal complex structures up to sign. The criterion combines the decomposition theorem of Druel–Guenancia–Paun, a Hilbert-polynomial index bound, and local positive-Ricci curvature; products of equal-dimensional projective spaces show that the strict threshold is sharp. For cubic n-folds with n at least 5, the note applies the criterion to identify all fibers of the forgetful map from complex-preserving GH moduli to ordinary metric GH moduli as conjugation orbits, including singular boundary points. This cubic application uses as an external input OpenAI's ordinary-double-point upper gap theorem at repository commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a; that theorem is not reproved here. The complex-preserving cubic GH/GIT comparison is an attributed deduction through Li–Liu's global Reeb minimum and Spotti–Sun's established transfer. Kong–Shen–Zhao–Zhao already publicly state a stronger complex algebraic comparison. Smooth tangent stability, smooth metric rigidity, and the conjugation convention are credited to Peternell–Wisniewski, Spotti, and Odaka–Spotti–Sun. metadata.title: Bilinear ergodic Hilbert variation for commuting transformations as a consequence of annular triangular variation
metadata.description: We give an explicit restriction and transference consequence of OpenAI's full annular variation theorem for the triangular Hilbert transform, manuscript dated October 5, 2026, at source commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. They have a bounded maximum and converge almost everywhere and in L^(3/2), with maximal-tail convergence in that norm. The proof uses fixed positive-area cell boxes, half-integer radial endpoints, an explicitly summable O(k^-2) signed kernel error, and finite-menu finite-window Calderon transference. metadata.title: Binary consequences of relation-liveness automata lower bounds
metadata.description: Explicit fixed-binary-alphabet consequences of OpenAI's two relation-liveness lower bounds. A strict h-squared adjacency-block language has a one-way nondeterministic source with (3h^3-h)/2+2 endmarked states, and an ordinary epsilon-free source with one fewer state. Equivalent two-way deterministic automata and two-way nondeterministic automata for its full binary complement require 2^Omega(h), hence 2^Omega(n^(1/3)) in the cubic source size. The note gives exact transitions, an sh^2-state pullback, all-word complement semantics, and an h^3 fooling-set source lower bound. The exponential obstructions are inherited from OpenAI; binary coding is established machinery, attributed to earlier work. AI tools were used extensively. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing. Automated proof and package audits are documented. Upstream Lean build, axiom printing and Comparator validation were not reproduced due local disk exhaustion; neither reproduced formal verification nor binary formalization is claimed.

metadata.title: A fixed moment separator without a rational normalized sum-of-squares certificate
metadata.description:
This research note exhibits the phenomenon asked about in the literal fixed-polynomial certificate question in Oberwolfach Report 14/2023, under an explicit rational polynomial-square convention. On the rational unit ball in three variables, p=1+f for Scheiderer's classical quartic has minimum one and annihilates an explicit rational degree-four moment vector of mass one. It belongs to 1+Q_R(g) but not to 1+Q_Q(g), even with arbitrary finite multiplier degrees. The input moment matrix is not positive semidefinite. A different polynomial q=1+x^4 certifies the same vector rationally, p itself is rationally positivity-certifiable, and every rational rescaling cp with c>1 has a rational normalized certificate. The result is outside the companion preprint's strict-margin regime and asserts no algorithm, minimal degree or general descent theorem.

The contribution is an explicit normalized-moment application and scope clarification of established ingredients. Scheiderer's quartic and field obstruction, the classical leading-form/completion mechanism, Benoist's formal-ring observation, Nie's earlier ball application, the prior irrational Gram and Naldi-Sinn semidefinite-infeasibility applications, and Powers' strictly positive rational certificate are credited. The portable archive supplies the manuscript source, all 35 exact rational moments and sparse polynomial data, a Python-standard-library checker with its complete byte-identical expected 2,059-check output, claim and priority notes, publication metadata, source-version provenance and a file-hash manifest. Finite computations supplement the written Galois and all-degree local proofs; they are not finite-search proofs of arbitrary-degree impossibility.

Three independently initiated bounded priority families identified no exact earlier normalized-moment application in the primary passages inspected. metadata.title: Nonconvexity of fixed odd-power sum-of-squares cones
metadata.description:
This research note gives a negative answer to the general-dimensional fixed odd-power convexity question recorded by Reznick in Oberwolfach Reports 14/2023 and repeated by Blekherman, Kozhasov and Reznick in 2026. For real nonnegative homogeneous sextics whose cubes are sums of squares, the cone is nonconvex in the explicit finite dimension 3*10^62: disjoint copies of the classical coefficient-1 modified Motzkin seed have SOS cubes, while their finite average does not. For every fixed odd exponent q>=3, some finite dimension n(q) gives nonconvexity. No ternary result, minimal dimension, uniform dimension for all exponents or full classification is claimed. Closedness and the earlier convexity of the union over odd exponents remain consistent.

The proof applies classical SOS separation, product truncated-functional positivity and elementary distinct-index counting. The exact seed, its SOS cube and the standard separation, tensor and collision ingredients are credited to earlier primary sources. An explicit rational order-nine moment functional yields the displayed dimension. The verification archive supplies the standalone manuscript source, all 20 initial minors and 24 exact Schur traces, a Python-standard-library checker with full 220 local LDL positivity/reconstruction, exact cube/moment/sign checks, complete expected output, hash/provenance records, claim scope and a dated priority note. metadata.title: A telescoping proof of the focal antipedal sum invariant
metadata.description:
This preprint proves the focal antipedal distance-sum equality observed by Reznik, Garcia and Koiller as elliptic billiard invariant k603. For every regular closed billiard/Poncelet orbit between strictly nested confocal ellipses, lambda strictly between zero and b squared, the ordinary positive radial-distance sums of the two focal antipedal polygons agree. The proof identifies their per-edge norm difference with a fixed coefficient times the vertical displacement, then uses closure. It covers odd primitive periods, admitted stars, reversal and repeated traversal, without asserting separate constancy of either sum or extending to hyperbolic or degenerate caustics. Standard-library exact rational-chord verification accompanies the self-contained proof.

metadata.title: NP-completeness of aggregate root-dependent spanning-tree cost
metadata.description:
For one common undirected spanning tree, every vertex root induces a whole-tree orientation whose arc costs are independently supplied. This preprint proves NP-completeness of deciding whether the sum of all root costs is at most a threshold, even with costs in {0,1,2}; a uniform shift gives costs in {1,2,3}. The self-contained satisfiability reduction resolves Problem 1 in Volker Kaibel's November 2018 Oberwolfach workshop contribution, whose report was published in December 2019. Standard-library exact verification files accompany the proof.

metadata.title: Measure-only preserving Markov transports characterize mass-stationarity
metadata.description:
This research note gives an affirmative answer to Last and Thorisson's formal Problem 7.3 (Annals of Probability, 2009). On any locally compact second countable Hausdorff Abelian group, for an arbitrary jointly measurable ambient flow, a sigma-finite measure Q and a nonzero covariant locally finite Radon random measure xi, full ambient invariance under every invariant xi-preserving xi-measurable Markov transport is equivalent to joint mass-stationarity. The proof derives the joint Mecke identity using oriented local symmetric transports away from measure periods and normalized period-subgroup transports. It requires neither a standard Borel ambient space, a sigma-finite marginal law of xi nor finite intensity. The classical Mecke/Palm and Palm/mass-stationarity equivalences and converse transport invariance are credited. The narrower non-discrete deterministic Cox-allocation converse is not claimed.

metadata.title: Exact chordal separation of spherical Fibonacci points
metadata.description:
This research note proves the exact finite separation conjecture stated in Johann S. Brauchart's OWR 40/2012 contribution, published in 2013. For every integer n at least 3, the rational unshifted unit-sphere configuration with Fn points has minimum Euclidean chord 2/sqrt(Fn), uniquely at the north pole and its first latitude point. A latitude-longitude inequality reduces the all-pair lower bound to classical Fibonacci dual-lattice arithmetic. An elementary unimodular-basis proof of the weaker arithmetic bound needed here makes the argument self-contained. The older construction, pole upper bound and Zaremba product index are credited. The theorem does not assert optimal sphere packing or apply to midpoint, irrational-angle or arbitrary-cardinality variants.

metadata.title: An explicit SU(5) lens-space counterexample to the printed Guadagnini-Pilo conjecture
metadata.description:
For the ordinary full SU(5) Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant at WZW level 5, shifted level 10, L(5,1) and L(5,2) have fundamental group Z/5 but unequal nonzero magnitudes. With S3 normalization equal to one, their squared magnitudes are 3475 + 1550 sqrt(5) and 4025 + 1800 sqrt(5). An exact A4 root-lattice reduction and reproducible cyclotomic certificates establish this counterexample to Conjecture 7.5 as printed on p.474 of Ohtsuki's collection (volume nominally 2002, published 1 June 2004), conditional on established full modular-category and RT/Hansen-Takata surgery inputs.

metadata.title: The mixed point spectrum of a matrix contraction on its closed unit ball
metadata.description:
We explicitly answer the mixed point-spectrum converse left open after Theorem 3.1.14(i) of Kari Valentina Kuster's 2015 thesis and stated only as an inclusion in her 2016 Pure Koopmanism contribution. For a matrix contraction on a finite-dimensional complex space with any complex norm, acting by composition on all continuous complex functions on its closed unit ball, every unimodular eigenfunction factors through the contractive peripheral spectral projection. The unimodular point spectrum is exactly the multiplicative group generated by the peripheral matrix eigenvalues. An elementary self-contained proof yields the full point and Banach-operator spectrum classification, including singular, nilpotent and nonnormal cases.

The missing exclusion is a short specialization of classical Jacobs-de Leeuw-Glicksberg theory and the prior all-peripheral calculation. The open-disk eigenvalues, prior peripheral and nilpotent cases, and the already immediate full-disk consequence are explicitly credited. metadata.title: Consistent spectral recovery of smooth reversible diffusion tensors at a fixed lag
metadata.description:
This research note proves almost-sure consistency of a specified finite-rank empirical spectral-equation estimator for a general smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic tensor and unknown positive smooth invariant density. The domain is known, bounded, connected and smooth, in dimension at least two. Observations are exact stationary positions at one known fixed positive lag, reflection is conormal, and fixed pointwise ellipticity and density bounds are known. The tensor and its separately fitted divergence converge locally uniformly; an ellipticity-clipped tensor converges globally in L2. The covariance is 2S/mu and the interior drift is (div S)/mu. The proof supplies boundary-corrected dependent-data kernel estimates, full spectral-jet excitation, continuous functional calculus through empirical spectral collisions and eigenvector-free measurability.

This supplies a convergence analysis for the smooth setting of the spectral reconstruction question posed by Reiss with Chorowski, Gobet and Hoffmann in OWR24/2017, published in 2018. Earlier general nonparametric spectral residual fitting and transition-eigenvalue power weighting by Crommelin and Vanden-Eijnden, reversible identification, scalar fixed-lag inference, cutoff spectral excitation, deterministic tensor reconstruction and classical elliptic regularity are credited. A bounded dated primary-source audit located no encompassing theorem, with explicit edition/access gaps including the uninspected Crommelin-Vanden-Eijnden 2011 publisher-final body; no worldwide firstness guarantee is made. The supplementary classical regularization application is a new derivation of another estimator during this audit, not an earlier published resolution or a proof of the spectral objective. metadata.title: A complete negatively curved observation Gramian with two-state ambiguity
metadata.description:
We give a nonvacuous two-dimensional counterexample to the manifold conjecture printed by Krener in OWR11/2009. A smooth observed system on a connected closed genus-three surface has zero dynamics and output in R17 obtained by composing a connected two-sheeted hyperbolic covering with a smooth Nash isometric embedding. Its exact finite-time differential observation Gramian is P_T=T*pi^*g. For every fixed positive T it is geodesically complete with actual sectional curvature -1/T and uniform positive upper and lower bounds relative to any fixed smooth background metric and a fixed finite normalized atlas. The history map is locally injective but every attained history has exactly two initial states.

The construction is an application of classical constructions, with Nash, covering classification, hyperbolic geometry and older local/global observability ambiguity explicitly credited. A bounded primary-source audit, including complete readings of Dirr2009 and Kang2013 and a fresh independent adversarial priority assessment, found no verified earlier explicit complete construction in inspected sources. metadata.title: Focal pedal area ratios of closed elliptic billiards
metadata.description:
This research note proves the focal pedal area equality observed by Reznik, Garcia and Koiller in April 2020 for every primitive closed elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate elliptical caustic, including coprime star orbits. More precisely, the signed supporting-line pedal areas of the outer tangent polygon and the original chord polygon are proportional by a positive phase-independent constant common to both foci. A common pair of simple poles, local original and adjacent outer cancellations, strict real signed positivity, and compact-torus residue matching yield the proof. Reversal and positive integral repetitions are covered explicitly.

An exact triangular certificate disproves the interpretation that the common focal ratio itself is constant over the family. Prior observation of the equality, its known primitive-even symmetry proof, an explicit triangular consequence of old geometric theorems, the classical nonconstancy corollary, canonical coordinates and established Jacobi principal-part methods are credited. The specialized local arguments already appeared in companion repository work and are reconstructed here. A bounded primary-source priority audit identified no earlier proof across the full stated domain; no absolute firstness, independently new invariant, triangular novelty, new negative theorem, or new general method is claimed. metadata.title: Asymptotic LOCC dense coding with the symmetric four-qubit W state
metadata.description:
We answer the historical distributed dense-coding question for the symmetric four-qubit W state in the local-unitary model of Bruss and collaborators. Two independent senders transmit one qubit each to different receivers. A complete Bell instrument at one receiver retains a classical-quantum output at the other; the established cq multiple-access coding theorem gives an achievable sum-rate supremum at least 3/2 + h2(1/4) = 2.311278124459... bits per resource copy. Both senders can achieve 9/8 bits per copy with vanishing uniform average error, establishing the original-model LOCC-DC classification.

The Bell decomposition, Bell forwarding, cqMAC coding theorem and prior general MAC dense-coding framework are explicitly credited. The bounded primary-literature audit found no earlier explicit or established-equivalent achievement of the exact target in inspected sources; specific access and version limitations are documented. metadata.title: Closedness and attractive approximation of binary MTP2 edge models
metadata.description:
For every fixed finite simple graph, this research note proves that the binary MTP2 probability distributions admitting finite nonnegative unary and original-edge factors are exactly the pointwise limits of strictly positive attractive Ising distributions on the same graph. It consequently answers Conjecture 1 in Lauritzen's 2022 Oberwolfach problem statement affirmatively, including zero probabilities and the source's literal edge-only conventions for isolated vertices and empty graphs. The proof explicitly handles pins, deterministic equalities and implication supports, aggregates interactions across equality classes, constructs positive attractive approximations, and uses a classical residual-flow representation to bound finite factors with a nonvanishing normalizer.

The note credits the toric support framework of Geiger, Meek and Sturmfels, the MTP2 graphical results of Lauritzen, Uhler and Zwiernik and Fallat et al., the natural-support factorization framework of Kahle and Sullivant, and classical graph-cut and residual-flow tools. The supplement gives the additional facial-lattice support derivation underlying the comparison. The accompanying negative answers to the separate factorization conjectures are credited to the exact earlier counterexample of Gandolfi and Lenarda, published April 13, 2017. No new-counterexample, first-discovery or exhaustive historical-priority claim is made. Portable exact verification code and generated results accompany the proofs; bounded finite checks do not replace the arbitrary-graph proof.

This is an unrefereed preprint. AI tools were used extensively in developing the arguments, searching primary literature, writing, coding, reproduction and independent adversarial review. metadata.title: Full 5-torsion of the regular-pentagon quintic pencil
metadata.description:
This research note computes all twenty-five geometric fifth-torsion points of the genus-one normalization of the regular-pentagon quintic pencil in McCallum's Question 17 in the AIM workshop problem list on rational and integral points. For an explicit equation normalization over K=Q(sqrt(5)), it gives a cubic model, both birational maps, a degree-ten residual polynomial and both ordinate branches. The complete division field is K(sqrt(5+2sqrt(5)),zeta_5,theta), where theta^5=lambda+phi^5 and phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2. Its degree is four or twenty, with the exact splitting criterion and Galois action specified. The computation covers every elliptic normalization, including the allowed cuspidal plane member.

The proof applies classical Tate normal form, Fisher's full-level modular cover, Verdure's full-torsion specialization criterion, Morton's prior explicit Tate torsion formulas and residual polynomial, division-polynomial theory and the Weil pairing. It credits the source's known infinity subgroup and the earlier partial computation. No first-discovery or first-priority claim is made. metadata.title: A counterexample to Takao's self-duality question
metadata.description:
For every prime p greater than 3 and every n at least 3, this research note constructs a finite flat commutative group scheme over W(closure of F_p), killed by p and of rank p^(2n), with quasi-supersingular special fiber, such that both the special fiber and its Witt-ring lift fail Cartier self-duality. It gives an explicit negative answer to the higher-rank question following Proposition 2 on page 2479 of Naotake Takao's contribution to Oberwolfach Report 42/2023.

The proof uses an explicit six-dimensional Dieudonne module, a supersingular elliptic p-torsion filtration, an image-intersection invariant and a finite Honda complement. These are applications of established Dieudonne and finite Honda theory, with the classical cyclic-word framework credited. No first-discovery or first-priority claim is made. metadata.title: Integer endpoint discontinuity of normalized uniformization for positively curved surfaces
metadata.description:

The critical r=1 case uses a small C^1 conformal correction controlling the full nonlinear inverse-coordinate curvature operator. This resolves the specified finite-integer endpoint question recorded in the 2017 Oberwolfach report, published on 3 January 2018.

The theorem concerns this specific normalized parametrization of smooth objects and makes no assertion about abstract homeomorphisms, RP^2, smooth or noninteger Holder topologies. metadata.title: An even-strand Markov calculus for classical and virtual links
metadata.description:

Four reversible algebraic schemes classify ordinary oriented unframed classical link closures using only even-strand braid states. Four additional exchange schemes give the corresponding statement for oriented virtual links. The proof converts the established unrestricted Markov theorems by positively stabilizing every odd-strand vertex and explicitly lifting every generating edge.

metadata.title: An alternating antimorphic Fine-Wilf theorem
metadata.description: For an arbitrary antimorphic involution theta, a finite word with alternating theta-periods p and q and length at least p+q-gcd(p,q) has alternating theta-period gcd(p,q). This proves the exact unnumbered conjecture after Theorem 23 on printed page 2220 of Nowotka's contribution, joint with Bischoff, to the 2010 Oberwolfach mini-workshop on combinatorics on words. The common finite extension theta(w)w has ordinary periods 2p and 2q; classical Fine-Wilf and central reflection give the alternating conclusion. A reversal example shows that the sufficient formula cannot be reduced by one uniformly; pairwise optimality is not asserted. The research note credits Fine and Wilf, the originating report and Bischoff's thesis, and compares the related Czeizler-Kari-Seki, Kari-Seki and Simpson results. metadata.title: Common L1 basin boundaries for a bistable mean-field interval map
metadata.description: We prove the common-basin-boundary conjecture stated by Keller in the 2009 Oberwolfach mini-workshop on the spectrum of transfer operators. For the prescribed two-branch Mobius interval maps with feedback G(m)=A tanh(Bm/A), A in (0,2/5] and B in (6,16], the basin of the constant density equals the boundary of each noncentral stable basin in the relative L1 topology of all probability densities. The central basin is also exactly the L1 closure of the finite preimages of the constant density. A terminal cumulative transport is lifted backward with self-consistent feedback; a probability-space inverse contraction and uniform distortion bound cover arbitrary integrable densities, including unbounded densities and densities with zeros. The global three-limit theorem, boundary seed, invariant integral representations and inverse-expansion mechanism are credited to Bardet, Keller and Zweimuller. metadata.title: The spatial locus of common tangents to three disjoint convex sets is null
metadata.description: Self-contained proof that the union of complete affine lines actually meeting three pairwise disjoint arbitrary convex subsets of R3 and contained in a supporting plane of each has Lebesgue outer measure zero. metadata.title: Non-symmetry of biconstrained two-step reachability
metadata.description: We give a negative answer to the symmetry question for the universal finite-tripartite biconstrained two-step reachability function psi: the absolute difference at (13/27,14/27) and its swap is at least 1/108. For rational theta in (0,1), we prove the exact boundary formula psi(1-theta,theta)=1-theta/d(theta), where d is a minimum integer degree over positively rational weighted regular incidence templates. The credited seven-type example of Chudnovsky, Hompe, Scott, Seymour and Spirkl and its complement bound the two relevant integers by four, which makes equality impossible. The exact values, their ordering and the invariant minima are not evaluated. A self-contained four-page research note and portable exact verification supplement accompany the result. The matrix and weighted framework are prior work. A dated bounded literature audit found no earlier equivalent theorem but does not certify global novelty; the cited 2019 senior thesis was inaccessible. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, literature research, writing and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not received external human peer review.

metadata.title: Fixed-generator positive factorizations in Wajnryb's Artin A5 quotient
metadata.description: We classify positive words in the five fixed standard generators of B6 modulo c=h representing c^2. The possible lengths are 20, 30 and 40, with respectively one, one and two strict Hurwitz classes. Simultaneous conjugation identifies the two length-40 classes, giving the three proposed representatives of Wajnryb's quotient question. A pure-braid linking reduction and an exhaustive exact 810-word certificate settle length 20. The classical group presentation, previously known length spectrum and Casson's twice-per-pair crossing assertion reported by Elrifai-Morton are explicitly credited. A full reproducible six-strand crossing certificate and independent controls accompany the note. Novelty of the exact complete classification is not certified by a negative literature search. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, literature research, writing and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not received external human peer review. The statement is restricted to fixed-generator input words, not arbitrary conjugate-factor or geometric factorizations.

metadata.title: A two-dimensional complex with embedding-dimension gap two
metadata.description:
This research note proves the existence of a finite two-dimensional simplicial complex with minimum piecewise-linear embedding dimension three and minimum original-simplex affine embedding dimension five. It answers affirmatively Brehm's 2006 question whether these minimum embedding dimensions can differ by more than one, already in dimension two. The first barycentric subdivision embeds linearly in three dimensions.

The argument makes a known balanced-Radon and random-complex affine obstruction uniform under all small facet deletions, then removes triangles sharing an edge. An elementary local-fan construction supplies the PL embedding. Existing Brehm–Sarkaria, Newman and Lee–Nevo methods are credited. Two independently fixed bounded literature audits found no checked theorem subsuming this exact result; categorical first priority is not asserted. Exact finite parameters and independent offline checks are supplied, but no explicit facet list for the enormous witness is generated. Finite checks supplement the universal proof and are not formal verification.

Generative AI tools were used extensively in problem solving, proof checking, literature review, manuscript preparation and independent adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint; no human peer review or formally machine-verified proof is claimed. Research prose is licensed CC BY4.0 and verification code MIT. The source-and-verification archive contains the manuscript source, pinned standard-library checks, provenance and source/priority evidence. The repository publication program records the separate fresh full preprint reviews.

metadata.title: Irreducibility of exposed-point varieties of discotopes
metadata.description:
This research note proves that the complex Zariski closure of the exposed points of every finite Minkowski sum of ellipsoidal discs of dimension at least two is irreducible, without genericity or full-dimensionality assumptions. It proves the exposed-point conjecture stated by Meroni in the 2023 Oberwolfach report. Under an explicit generic condition on summand spans, it also proves equality with the purely nonlinear part of Gesmundo and Meroni, resolving their 2022 irreducibility conjecture. A nongeneric example distinguishes the two varieties.

The proof combines a connected real-analytic support-point parametrization with a standard analytic irreducibility lemma. Earlier partial discotope results and the analytic precursor are credited. Historical first priority is not asserted. The source-and-verification archive includes the manuscript source, pinned exact checks, provenance, a dated priority audit, and independent adversarial reviews. Finite symbolic checks corroborate formulas and examples; they do not replace the universal proofs.

Generative AI tools were used extensively in proof development, literature triage, manuscript preparation, adversarial review, and symbolic-check design. This is an unrefereed preprint; no human peer review or formal proof certification is claimed. Research prose is licensed CC BY 4.0 and verification code is licensed MIT.

metadata.title: Nonattainment in the Harrell–Stubbe Dirichlet gap inequality
metadata.description:
We prove that the universal Harrell–Stubbe gap bound for Dirichlet eigenvalues is never attained on a nonempty bounded open subset of Euclidean space at any finite index. More strongly, Yang's first inequality is strict at every real threshold above the lowest eigenvalue. The proof uses the classical spectral remainder and a self-adjointness obstruction to finite spectral support of a coordinate times an eigenfunction. No boundary regularity or connectedness is required.

This answers the corrected saturation question recorded in the 2009 Oberwolfach report and listed as OWR-3389-016; the original report's missing square is explicitly documented. The package includes the paper, LaTeX source, independent AI-assisted proof audits, a scoped priority audit, and a dependency-free verifier with 7,016 exact checks. The computation checks algebra and box spectra, not the general analytic theorem. No earlier explicit nonattainment proof was located in the literature checked; this is not an exhaustive priority certification. Research and writing were AI-assisted.
metadata.notes: Original manuscript and documentation: CC BY 4.0. Verification and build code: MIT (see LICENSES.md). No external peer-review or proof-assistant certification is claimed.

metadata.title: Radial orthogonality does not imply dual 1-conformal flatness
metadata.description:
We give an explicit negative answer to Takashi Kurose's Question 3(e) in Furuhata, Matsuzoe and Urakawa, Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics (1998), p.126, indexed as AMR-059-0011 / 6000011. On the product S^2(1) x R with its product metric and Levi-Civita connection, every radial orthogonal distribution in the question is integrable, but the dual statistical structure is nowhere locally 1-conformally flat. The proof combines the first variation of energy with two incompatible curvature evaluations. A conformal metric and projective connection deformation yields a non-self-dual example with nowhere zero cubic tensor; the product obstruction extends to every dimension at least three.

The package contains a four-page manuscript, LaTeX source, a standard-library exact rational verifier, an independently implemented SymPy verifier, source and priority audits, and reproducibility instructions. The computations supplement the analytic proof. Historical priority remains unresolved. The documented, bounded search found no earlier explicit answer, but relevant sources remain uninspected, including Kurose's 1999 affine-realization paper, Binder-Simon's 2000 problem list, and the full content of Kurose's 2016 talk. An earlier answer or implicit resolution in those sources cannot be excluded. No first-resolution claim or assertion that the question remained open at publication is made. The ingredients are classical; the exact deformation is credited to Matsuzoe (1999), p.178, equation (2.1).

This is an unrefereed, AI-assisted preprint. The candidate was supplied as AI-generated work. The manuscript, verification materials, and separate adversarial AI audits were prepared with OpenAI Codex. AI reviews are not external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.
metadata.notes: Text is CC BY 4.0; original Python code is MIT licensed as specified in LICENSES.md. No third-party source PDFs are redistributed. The publication date is the manuscript date in America/Los_Angeles.

metadata.title: A note on Γ-supercyclicity of dissipative composition operators
metadata.description:
This research note records an affirmative answer to the arbitrary-Gamma supercyclicity question in Emma D'Aniello's contribution (joint work with Martina Maiuriello), p.1083 of Oberwolfach Report 19/2024. In the report's separable complex Lp setting, 1 <= p < infinity, a dissipative composition operator of bounded distortion is Gamma-supercyclic if and only if its associated bilateral weighted shift is Gamma-supercyclic, for every subset Gamma of the complex numbers.

The note makes explicit an application of earlier results of Arafat Abbar (2019) and Arafat Abbar and Yulia Kuznetsova (2020 preprint; 2021 journal article). It includes a direct proof and a deduction from the earlier translation theorem. Neither the scalar criterion nor the amplification mechanism is claimed as new. The original separability assumption is retained explicitly.

This is an AI-assisted, unrefereed research note, not an external peer-review or formal proof-assistant certificate. The deposit contains the PDF and self-contained LaTeX source archive.

metadata.title: The odd-part ratio under slow variation: a note on the printed Hilberdink problem
metadata.description:
For every nonzero nonnegative multiplicative function f whose summatory function F is slowly varying, the odd-part ratio F2(x)/F(x) converges to the reciprocal of the unweighted local sum sum(k>=0) f(2^k), with reciprocal infinity interpreted as zero. A short monotonicity proof covers finite and infinite local sums and bounded summatory functions.

This answers the existence question under the slow-variation hypothesis printed in Hilberdink's Problem 3 in Oberwolfach Report 51/2017 and catalogued as OWR-15956-012. The source's accompanying weighted numerical prediction is incompatible with that hypothesis: f(n)=1/n gives actual limit 1/2, whereas that prediction gives 3/4. The possible intended index-one regular-variation problem is not resolved here.

The deposit includes a three-page paper, editable LaTeX, exact finite-check Python code, independent AI proof audits, a source audit, and a bounded priority-search record. No exact earlier resolution was found in the searched literature; originality is not certified, and limitations in full-text access are recorded. Finite computation supplements the analytic proof and is not formal proof-assistant verification.
references: F. Bayart, K. Matomäki, E. Saksman, K. Seip (organizers), Mini-Workshop: Interplay between Number Theory and Analysis for Dirichlet Series, Oberwolfach Reports 14 (2017), no. 4, 3035–3069; Problem 3 (T. Hilberdink), pp. 3065–3066. DOI: 10.4171/OWR/2017/51.
K. Yeats, Asymptotic Density in Combined Number Systems, New York Journal of Mathematics 8 (2002), 63–83.
K. Yeats, A Multiplicative Analogue of Schur's Tauberian Theorem, Canadian Mathematical Bulletin 46 (2003), no. 3, 473–480. DOI: 10.4153/CMB-2003-046-5.

metadata.title: Equality in the Fradelizi–Paouris–Schütt second-moment inequality
metadata.description:
Fradelizi, Paouris, and Schütt proved a sharp lower bound for the normalized second moment of a convex body whose extreme points have Euclidean norm at least r, and characterized equality for polytopes. This note proves their conjectured characterization for arbitrary convex bodies: equality in C₂(K) ≥ [r²+(n+1)‖g_K‖²]/(n+2) holds exactly for nondegenerate simplices with all vertices of norm r. The proof covers every dimension n≥1 and resolves the mathematical question catalogued as OWR-4136-011.

The four-page proof uses an almost-everywhere extreme-point simplex partition and an exact nonnegative deficit identity. A retained-pair estimate supplies a second finite-approximation route. The deposit includes LaTeX source, an exact standard-library Python verifier, independent AI proof audits, a source comparison, and a bounded priority search. All 298 finite checks across 18 cases pass; they do not replace the analytic proof. No earlier resolution was found in the searched literature, without certifying global priority. This is an unrefereed, AI-assisted preprint. Text is CC BY 4.0; code is MIT.
metadata.notes: Prepared with OpenAI Codex from a candidate supplied by the author from prior AI-assisted work, with separate AI verification agents. The inequality, simplex moment identity, and polytope equality case are due to Fradelizi, Paouris, and Schütt; the contribution is the general-convex-body equality classification. The audits are not external human peer review.

metadata.title: A coefficient normalization for positive definite forms
metadata.description:
Every positive definite real homogeneous form of positive degree admits an invertible real linear change of variables in which the symmetric ordered coefficients have diagonal entries equal to one and every mixed entry strictly between zero and one. This gives an affirmative answer to Brandes's Problem 11 in the 2019 Oberwolfach report on Analytic Number Theory, including the printed absolute-value inequality.

The three-page proof clusters a basis near a direction minimizing the form on a Euclidean sphere. A polynomial gap has a strictly positive quadratic term for every mixed tuple. The accompanying source package includes an independent proof via positive definite bilinear slices and Cauchy-Schwarz, internal adversarial audits including three fresh preprint-readiness rounds and independently rechecked supplementary controls, a dated priority search, and a standard-library Python verifier with exact rational certificates. The finite checks supplement the analytic proof and are not a formal verification of the universal theorem.

Brandes's 2015 discussion of pseudo-diagonal forms is credited as a direct precursor. A bounded literature audit found no earlier full resolution; first priority is not established. This is an unrefereed preprint developed and checked with generative-AI assistance. Paper and prose: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT.

metadata.title: A Lipschitz-nonincreasing deformation of small unitary-valued maps
metadata.description:
For the unit-round sphere and either the unnormalized Hilbert–Schmidt or operator-norm length metric on U(N), this note gives an explicit strong deformation retraction of the maps with Lipschitz constant at most 1/2 onto the constant maps. At time t in [0,1], the Lipschitz constant is at most (1-t²)/(1+t²) times its original value. The formula is continuous in the entire input map, fixes constant maps, preserves the strict sublevel, and stays in the original U(N). It supplies an affirmative answer to the literal assertion in Gromov’s 2017 question [?24](i), catalogued as AMR-066-0025.

The proof is elementary matrix algebra plus an intrinsic curve-length argument. The Cayley/Möbius transformation is classical. Ordinary contraction without preservation of the Lipschitz sublevel already follows from a standard logarithm chart. A documented, bounded literature search located no earlier explicit resolution or exact quantitative map-space retraction; first-publication priority is not established.

The package includes the four-page preprint, editable LaTeX source, independent AI-assisted internal reviews, a priority audit, dependency-free exact algebra checks, optional NumPy stress tests, and SHA-256 checksums. The scripts are finite diagnostics, not a formal proof of the theorem. This is an unrefereed preprint developed and checked with generative-AI assistance. Paper and prose: CC BY 4.0; code: MIT.

metadata.title: A four-vertex counterexample to Knudson's persistence-gradient conjecture
metadata.description:
Knudson conjectured that every nonincident persistence pair is joined by exactly one gradient path in the discrete vector field obtained by retaining the incident persistence pairs. This note gives a simplex-wise filtration of a triangulated interval with four vertices and three edges for which one such pair has no gradient path. It disproves Conjecture 2 in Knudson's contribution to Oberwolfach Report 29/2008, p. 1629. The proof consists of three boundary reductions and an inspection of the matching, and the same example works over any field.

The deposit includes a three-page manuscript, LaTeX source, two exact standard-library Python verifiers, original inputs, and mathematical and priority audit notes. A bounded literature search located no earlier explicit refutation, without guaranteeing historical novelty. This is an unrefereed, AI-assisted preprint; the audits are not external human peer review. Text is CC BY 4.0; code is MIT.

metadata.title: A counterexample to Kourovka Notebook Problem 16.45
metadata.description:
We construct an explicit affine group G = F_29^2 semidirect H, with H isomorphic to SL_2(5), of order 100920 for which b_f(G) = b(G) = 3 < 4 = mu′(G). Here b(G) is the largest size of an inclusion-minimal base over all permutation representations, including nonfaithful and intransitive actions, and mu′(G) is the largest size of an independent subset, whether or not it generates G. This gives a negative answer to P. J. Cameron's Kourovka Notebook Problem 16.45.

The upper bound is structural and does not enumerate the full subgroup lattice of the affine group. Every subgroup missing the translation subgroup has faithful base invariant at most two, and every nontrivial normal subgroup contains the translations. Explicit witnesses attain both bounds. The intersection associated with the independent four-set is a nonnormal subgroup of order two, exposing the normal-bottom obstruction.

This record contains the revised preprint and its self-contained source and verification archive: editable LaTeX, exact group specifications, certificates, standard-library Python and C++17 verifiers, an additional independently written checker, research provenance, and separate structural, computational, and primary-source audit reports. Exact checks reconstruct all 76 complement subgroups, check 1215450 four-member families and 67525 three-member families, and verify the affine witnesses and the characteristic-11 boundary example.

Author: Alec Kriebel (ORCID 0009-0001-9320-500X). This publication revision and its verification were prepared with OpenAI Codex and separate AI audit agents. One matrix-product order was corrected from six to three; the generated subgroup still has order twelve, and the theorem is unchanged. No unresolved substantive gap was identified within the recorded audit scope. This is an unrefereed preprint, not external human peer review or complete proof-assistant verification. The foundational formulations are attributed to Cameron, including his published 2024 account. No minimum-order claim is made, and the bounded priority search does not guarantee novelty.

Version 1.0.1 clarifies the projective-pair and intersection-order arguments and prevents obsolete output files from entering rebuilt upload kits. The mathematical construction and theorem are unchanged. The source package includes two new sequential adversarial reviews and the disposition of their findings. The second fresh reviewer found zero actionable issues after the repairs.

metadata.title: An explicit odd-order p-group with as many automorphisms as elements
metadata.description:
We construct an explicit nontrivial finite p-group G of odd order with p = 1009 and |G| = |Aut(G)| = 1009^52359, giving an affirmative answer to D. MacHale’s problem 16.63 in the Kourovka Notebook. Here Aut(G) is the full automorphism group.

The group is obtained by the finite Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff construction from an explicitly specified rank-31 Lie ring modulo 1009^1689. Its nilpotency class is at most 846 < 1009. An asymmetric lattice and a rigid finite-field flag force every finite Lie-ring automorphism into an integral logarithm–exponential domain. A precision-preserving bijection then identifies the full automorphism set with the kernel of an exact derivation matrix. Its rank is 931, its nullity is 30, and its nonzero 1009-primary Smith valuations have multiplicities 87, 55, 758, 6, and 25 at valuations 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4. Their sum is 1689. The finite Lazard correspondence preserves the full automorphism group and completes the group-theoretic conclusion.

This record contains the unrefereed preprint and its focused companion archive: editable LaTeX, the explicit group specification, exact certificates, verification software, computational logs, and scoped AI audit reports. The underlying Lie-algebra template is credited to Omirov and Ruan, arXiv:2605.04602v1, Theorem 4.8. Version 1.1.0 adds artifact citations, two mathematical clarifications, and publication-disclosure improvements; the mathematical construction and computational data are unchanged.

The construction, proof development, and initial verification software were generated using ChatGPT-6 Astra Pro. Separate Codex sessions performed additional AI-assisted reviews and exact computational checks. All checks described in the accompanying audits were completed, with no unresolved error identified within their stated scope. These checks do not constitute external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization. No minimality claim is made for the prime or group order.

metadata.title: Raw Strongly Tree-Child Level-2 Species Networks from Metric Genealogy Laws under the NMSC: Signed pair co-occupancy, rooted graph reconstruction, and demographic fibers
metadata.description:
We classify the observable rooted graph and parameters of finite strict temporally separated binary strongly tree-child species networks of level at most two under the independent-lineage Network Multispecies Coalescent (NMSC), with a fixed known surjective taxon sampling map. Equality of complete normalized rooted metric-genealogy laws is equivalent, pointwise on the full positive domain, to an explicit quotient generated by eight move types.

The proof recovers current pair co-occupancy from the analytic germ of a finite positive Kingman mixture. Signed jumps reveal every tree event and every pair-exposed reticulation. Descendant clusters, chronology, tree-childness and level-two shortcut completion then reconstruct the retained graph, including arbitrary decorations. Deterministic witnesses and actual three-lineage merger densities recover oriented inheritance weights and the entire finite demographic rate words on exposed populations. Scalar propagation through ancestral reticulations links both incoming arms, including equal rates and inheritance one-half. The indexed collection of all genealogy marginals on at most three sampled lineages suffices for the complete quotient.

A reticulation with one descendant sampled lineage retains its two typed first-exposure outlets and route weights, while its internal clock and singly occupied demographic words are unobservable. Sister-transfer direction is invisible exactly when both sides are sample unary; the corresponding reversal transfers the whole exposed donor rate word. Together with presentation suppression, equal-rate composition, unary-corridor replacement, parent exchange and labelled isomorphism, these responses exhaust the quotient. Exact hidden-clock and rank-one nonbridge examples explain essential obstructions. A separate graph argument derives the five cores and twelve minimum strong repairs.

The companion study transfers the classification to all indexed ordered locus laws with known boundaries, jointly with the stationary distribution and trace-normalized shared irreducible stationary reversible substitution generator. The reconstruction uses observable current-grouping scalars throughout.

Notes: Version 1.0.0 preprint, manuscript dated 5 September 2026. The accompanying files contain the main paper, technical supplement, manuscript sources, and curated reproducibility materials with exact technical checks. The three-lineage result concerns the indexed collection of all marginals on at most three sampled lineages of the same fixed known sampling design; it is a sufficient bound, with no claim of sharpness or recovery from one fixed triple. The sequence corollary uses the companion paper Direct Sequence Laws under the Network Multispecies Coalescent.

metadata.title: Direct Sequence Laws under the Network Multispecies Coalescent: A genealogy equivalence, canonical coalescent-response behavior, and finite determination with an epoch-complexity obstruction
metadata.description:
We determine the exact population-level information in multilocus sequence alignments generated by a temporal species network under the independent-lineage Network Multispecies Coalescent (NMSC), without treating estimated gene trees or concordance factors as observed data. With known nonrecombining locus boundaries, contemporaneous labelled sampling, and one shared irreducible stationary reversible finite-state continuous-time Markov chain, the indexed family of length-L locus laws is equivalent to the stationary distribution, the trace-normalized substitution generator, and the mutation-scaled metric-genealogy law. The first step is a compact moment theorem for the random conditional site-pattern tensor. A determinant coordinate then recovers each realized additive gene-tree metric, while a continuum in the ancestral coalescence tail identifies the shared generator, including JC, K2P, K3P, and repeated-eigenvalue GTR strata.

We compile every finite temporal NMSC presentation into a finite typed continuous-time response system on partition–occupancy states. Its canonical reachable–observable residual behavior, denoted CCR, is coordinate independent, removes analytically invisible event times, and is unique up to typed linear isomorphism. Equality of CCR is equivalent to equality of normalized metric-genealogy laws. The minimal time-indexed realization has an intrinsic positive cone, but its finite analytic encoding does not supply a stochastic occupancy basis or an NMSC graph. Literal graph recovery is impossible on the strict physical domain: arbitrary sample-unary temporal funnels have identical response in every context. Species trees are nevertheless recovered pointwise with all exposed population rates. For one-reticulation presentations we give an exact finite port-response quotient and a graph theorem on the incidence-separated subclass; the reduced level-1 result additionally assumes scalar-separator faithfulness, and no unconditional level-1 or level-2 graph theorem is claimed.

The finite-locus hierarchy has two complementary conclusions. On every fixed finite union of compact semianalytic finite-presentation charts, one finite locus length determines the complete indexed family. The proof uses the Frisch–Siu Noetherian ring of analytic germs along a compact set and remains valid at coalescent–substitution resonances. No determining length can depend only on the number of sampled taxa, reticulations, alphabet size, and sampling design if demographic epoch count is unbounded. For every L we construct two strict two-taxon, zero-reticulation, known-JC demographic histories with identical laws through length L and different length-(L+1) laws. A Vandermonde Jacobian and the implicit-function theorem make the collision exact. We finally separate Borel inversion, finite proposed-model equivalence testing, moment approximation, and statistical consistency.

Notes: Version 1.0.0 preprint, manuscript dated 5 September 2026. The accompanying files contain the main paper, technical supplement, manuscript sources, and curated reproducibility materials with exact technical checks. The main observation is the indexed family of ordered locus laws with known locus boundaries; the graph conclusions retain the qualifications stated in the paper.

metadata.title: Exact Diffusion Design for Maximally Collective Stable Turing Patterns in Binary-Complex Mass-Action Networks
metadata.description:
For every n ≥ 4, this preprint constructs an n-species binary-complex classical mass-action topology for which, throughout every positive-equilibrium realization, every principal subsystem below order n − 1 is Hurwitz while one order-(n − 1) subsystem is unstable. A general principal-minor diffusion-ray theorem yields an exact network law: for any homogeneously stable realization, a stationary crossing occurs along a positive diagonal diffusion ray exactly when d_Z > 8 h_Z Σ_{j=2}^{n−2} d_j/h_j. This gives the nonattained fixed-equilibrium contrast infimum, the unit-equilibrium value 8(n − 3), and the topology-wide stationary trade-off χ_D χ_H > 8(n − 3).

At unit equilibrium, an exact rational design undergoes a primary supercritical bifurcation with locally exponentially stable positive patterns in the fixed-integrated-mass class. A second exact family redistributes heterogeneity between diffusion and equilibrium concentrations so that both contrasts are Θ(√n), matching the topology-specific stationary minimax lower bound in exponent. The proof uses explicit flux-cone design, exhaustive strongly connected block classification, conservation-compatible center-manifold reduction, and inspectable symbolic certificates.

The networks are synthetic. The bifurcation, stability, and robustness conclusions are local for each fixed dimension, and the stationary diffusion law does not classify arbitrary wave instability. This is a submission-ready author preprint and has not undergone journal peer review.

Version 1.0.11 includes the main preprint, mathematical supplement, self-contained TeX source, portable exact-verification repository, and a separate data archive. The exact companion software release is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22625980.

metadata.title: Symmetry-Stratified Identifiability of Strongly Tree-Child Level-2 Phylogenetic Networks: A Unified Theory for JC, K2P, and K3P
metadata.description:
The classical four-state group-based DNA models form three symmetry strata on G = Z₂ × Z₂: Jukes–Cantor (JC), Kimura 2-parameter (K2P), and Kimura 3-parameter (K3P) tie the three nonzero Fourier characters in one, two, and three blocks, respectively. Using exact version-bound results from three companion classifications, this work gives a unified theorem for leaf-labelled binary standard semi-directed strongly tree-child networks of level at most two. On the strict principal positive-eigenvalue domain, and separately in strict edgewise continuous time, a source-relative regular full-dimensional containment from N to N′ on the same finite labelled leaf set exists exactly when the networks differ only by coherent ordinary-triangle redirection. The same condition characterizes a common regular germ full-dimensional in both images. Consequently, under any one known fixed model, a generic exact complete leaf site-pattern distribution identifies the same triangle-redirection quotient among networks in this class on the same leaf set.

The synthesis also proves uniform three-leaf triangle geometry. With r ∈ {1,2,3} character-tying blocks, the normalized ambient dimension is a_r = r(r+7)/2, the Jacobian rank is d_r = 5r−1, the regular local fibre dimension under the standard six-edge triangle parameterization is r+2, and the ambient codimension is binomial(r−1,2). It interprets the K3P H₁₄ conormal through the sign representation, proves that full-dimensional containment cannot point from a richer classical model to a poorer one, establishes monotone target-model refinement for triangle-equivalent networks, and classifies all 144 ordered cross-model relations among the labelled three-leaf tree and three ordinary-sunlet orientations. Strong tree-childness is shown to be a sharp class-level boundary through model-specific weak-class examples.

The reproducibility package contains the article, technical supplement, source, four exact bounded replays, deterministic build files, verification manifests, dependency bindings, and provenance. The replays check the synthesis-specific finite and symbolic calculations; the imported global JC, K2P, K3P, and tree–theta results remain bound to their separate DOI records.

The paper does not claim equality of complete stochastic images, boundary coverage, recovery under an unknown substitution model, bounded finite-sample sufficiency, complete numerical-parameter identification, all binary level-2 networks, or level-3 results.

metadata.title: Triangle Hypersurfaces and a Sharp Identifiability Boundary for Level-2 K3P Networks
metadata.description:
We classify regular full-dimensional stochastic containment among binary standard semi-directed strongly tree-child level-2 phylogenetic networks under the Kimura three-parameter (K3P) model. On the principal positive Fourier domain, a directed containment germ exists if and only if the labelled reduced trees of blobs agree and corresponding complete factors are either labelled-isomorphic or ordinarily triangle-redirected, with coherent boundary transports. The same condition is equivalent to a common full-dimensional regular germ and remains exact in strict continuous time. Thus no proper one-sided containment occurs in the strong class, and the semi-directed topology is generically identifiable and exactly reconstructible outside a proper exceptional set, modulo ordinary triangle redirection.

The three ordinary K3P triangle orientations have generic normalized rank 14, share the same irreducible eight-term quartic hypersurface H₁₄ in normalized three-leaf Fourier space, and meet in a common strict continuous-time smooth rank-14 germ. The bounded residue consists of fourteen four-port directed relation orbits—nine polynomially separated and five directed-rank separated—plus two separately separated sink swaps. Exact restoration and coherent one- and two-port probes extend the bounded classification to arbitrary labelled subdivision words.

Strong tree-childness is sharp against weakening to weak tree-childness. For every n ≥ 3, two weakly but not strongly tree-child networks have strict continuous-time K3P images sharing a common full-dimensional regular germ of dimension 6n − 3.

This is the first Zenodo/DOI-bearing archival release of version 1.0.0 of the complete K3P level-2 classification and its reproducibility evidence. It contains the article, reader supplement, compile-complete source archives, canonical full proof archive, compact verifier, independent-referee replay package, exact manifest, checksums, citation metadata, and a file-level license notice. The deposited bytes correspond to immutable Git commit 0b76dd8e38f262ebe9ba8c1d23281853e334fef2, annotated tag k3p-level2-identifiability-v1.0.0 resolving to that commit, and full-archive SHA-256 4f84417f40b4e5ddae80b36d87dc7bb6d00389a573a58d0b82a2592c9f7c6403.

metadata.title: Generic Identifiability and Directed Containment for Strongly Tree-Child Level-2 Networks under the Kimura Two-Parameter Model: The Principal Positive Domain and Strict Continuous Time
metadata.description:
We classify regular full-dimensional stochastic containment among binary standard semi-directed strongly tree-child level-2 phylogenetic networks under the Kimura two-parameter (K2P) model. On the principal positive Fourier domain D₊ = {(s,g): 0<s<1, 0<g<1, g>2s−1}, a directed containment germ exists if and only if the two labelled networks are isomorphic after independently redirecting ordinary three-cycle factors. The same condition is equivalent to a common full-dimensional regular germ; in particular, no proper one-sided containment occurs. It follows that the semi-directed topology is generically identifiable modulo ordinary triangle redirection, and that its structural triangle class is exactly reconstructible away from a proper algebraic exceptional set.

The proof combines displayed-quartet inequalities and exact whole-map identities, an exact two-sector bridge-fibre theorem, physical marginal submersions, localization, and a bounded graph-to-algebra classification of cycle and theta factors. The bounded classification is computer-assisted: every directed primitive relation, rank exclusion, restoration parent, transport, and one-/two-port probe is represented by an exact certificate with independent replay and mutation evidence. The classification transfers to the strict continuous-time domain 0<s<1, s²<g<1. For every n≥3, two weakly but not strongly tree-child level-2 networks have continuous-time K2P images sharing a regular germ of dimension 4n−3, proving sharpness of strong tree-childness.

This record is the complete v1.0.5-r1 priority and reproducibility package: the 26-page article, 24-page reader supplement, compile-complete five-file source archive, deterministic 495-member referee/verifier archive, external archive-qualification report, checksum sidecars, and dual-license notice. metadata.title: Exact Tree–Theta-Trinet Collisions under the Kimura 2- and 3-Parameter Models
metadata.description:
We construct exact distributions shared by a phylogenetic tree and a binary semi-directed strict level-two theta network under the Kimura two-parameter (K2P) and three-parameter (K3P) substitution models. The compact three-leaf K2P construction lies in the strict stochastic interior and is an exact counterexample to the formal K2P lemma and the K2P part of the corresponding global corollary removed between Versions 2 and 3 of Brits, Holtgrefe, van Iersel, and Martin. Because K2P is nested in K3P, this collision alone answers both high-level Kimura tree–trinet disjointness questions posed in Version 3 negatively. We additionally give an exact K3P theta realization whose network parameter lies outside every globally character-relabelled K2P specialization, while openly identifying its shared distribution as globally character-relabelled K2P. Full-rank Jacobians show that the fixed theta images are Zariski dense in the effective K2P and K3P Fourier spaces. Locally, the collision loci have dimensions 17 and 23 and project submersively onto the tree models, with 11- and 14-dimensional fixed-output network fibers. Consequently, a relatively open dense set of nearby K3P tree distributions outside every globally character-relabelled K2P submodel also has theta realizations. These conclusions persist in edgewise strictly continuous-time chambers, where generators and rate ratios may vary by edge and no clock or global timing is imposed. Finally, a common-subtree argument replaces any chosen internal vertex of any labelled unrooted binary tree by one theta blob while preserving the full leaf-pattern distribution; hence exact strict-interior collisions occur for every number of leaves. For the compact K2P and quartic K3P witnesses, exact verifiers separately reconstruct the retained-graph Fourier coordinates and perform ordinary-state Markov pruning in every pattern.

Preprint; not peer reviewed by a journal. This record archives version 1.2.7 of the full manuscript together with its exact certificates, standard-library verifiers, replay transcripts, source files, and integrity manifests. The deposited files correspond to Git commit 19cf11f65ed448cf031842b666e4bfc7e02a9ab7 and canonical archive SHA-256 7c603e15f6afb7546f618b88bbefdc52ee264b656399f6656fc742aeabb786c7. AI-assisted exploratory analysis, code assistance, adversarial checking, and editorial review are disclosed in the manuscript's “Provenance and AI-assisted methods” section.

metadata.title: A fitness-independent family of simultaneous amplifiers beyond relative fitness 3/2
metadata.description:
We study fixation from a uniformly random single mutant on finite connected loopless undirected weighted graphs under both Birth–death (Bd) and death–Birth (dB) Moran updating. Let R_sim be the supremum of R for which one fitness-independent graph family eventually amplifies fixation under both rules for every fixed r in (1,R). Let R_hyb be the unique root in (3/2,151/100) of

R^6 − 8R^5 + 22R^4 − 30R^3 + 21R^2 − 6R + 1.

We construct one fitness-independent family that simultaneously amplifies every fixed 1 < r < R_hyb for all sufficiently large members of the sequence. Therefore R_sim ≥ R_hyb = 1.5028569127905696… > 3/2.

The construction combines a large clique with dilute hub pendants and dilute, internally heavy two-vertex satellites. An exact finite-state derivation of the weak-cut limiting trace, together with uniform establishment, cleanup, and reciprocal-invasion estimates at the scale of the eventual gain, reduces the two normalized fixation corrections to explicit response functions. Optimizing their common positivity interval yields the displayed sextic. The same analysis proves that R_hyb is optimal among fixed positive (sigma, lambda) in the displayed first-order dilute pair–pendant response model; a specialization with entirely rational edge weights already crosses 3/2. Thus 3/2 is not the exact simultaneous-amplification threshold. The unrestricted value of R_sim, and even a finite universal upper bound, remain open.

Version note

Version 2.0.4, August 2026. This is an unrefereed preprint. It supersedes the earlier v1 source/software archive at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21852072.

This record contains the preprint and its complete source-and-certificate archive. The supplied exact verifiers replay the finite symbolic, rational, and finite-state calculations. The weak-cut and population asymptotics are analytic proofs in the manuscript and are not claimed as computer-assisted consequences of the replay.

metadata.title: Local Complete-Graph Optimality at Fitness Two and Strong-Selection Rigidity under Death–Birth Updating
metadata.description: We study fixation from a uniformly random single mutant under death–Birth updating on finite loopless directed weighted population structures. After normalizing each target’s incoming weights, the dynamics are parametrized by a loopless row-stochastic replacement kernel; let J_n denote the uniform complete kernel. We prove two complementary extremality results. First, at mutant fitness two, J_n is a strict nondegenerate local maximizer in the full normalized kernel polytope for every n ≥ 3. This includes arbitrary directed and nonreversible perturbations. The proof represents the fixation committor as a completely alternating coverage function of a fair-geometric union dual, converts fixation into a stationary collision observable, and decomposes the inverse-mean Hessian into standard, symmetric-balanced, and antisymmetric-balanced permutation sectors with positive sector certificates valid for every population size, using exact rational computer assistance over an explicitly finite range. Second, we close the complete-support case left outside the prior strongly connected noncomplete-support obstruction. The leading strong-selection deficit is an explicit sum of squared discrepancies within incoming columns, with equality exactly at J_n after normalization. Together with the prior obstruction and a source-component bound, this shows that no fixed finite directed weighting is a strict amplifier for every beneficial fitness. We also prove global all-beneficial-fitness maximality for positive weighted triangles and within two symmetric weighted K_4 families. These results establish strict local rigidity at fitness two and fixed-graph rigidity at strong selection, but not global complete-graph maximality at fitness two.

metadata.title: Positive Recurrence for Single-Linkage Bimolecular Weakly Reversible Stochastic Reaction Networks
metadata.description:
Stochastic mass-action reaction networks are chemical-master-equation models of low-copy-number biochemical systems. Anderson and Kim conjectured that weak reversibility implies positive recurrence. We prove this for finite bimolecular networks with one linkage class, removing the earlier requirement that every species occur in a pure unary or pure-double complex. Under weak reversibility, the states reachable from each initial population form a closed communicating class. Under the additional one-linkage and bimolecular hypotheses, for every positive rate vector each nonabsorbing reachable class is positive recurrent, whereas an absorbing singleton carries its point-mass law; consequently every reachable class has a unique stationary probability distribution. The closure statement follows by lifting directed return paths of complexes to population states.

For recurrence, the proof marks the target of the most recently fired channel and applies a log-factorial potential after subtracting that target. Its increment is exactly the logarithm of a target/source falling-factorial ratio, so following the carried target has zero reward. Finite target-following paths propagate the negative drift of a rare terminal source, while a normalized-log compactification and a bimolecular top-complex alternative rule out all other divergent sequences. The same return-cycle construction recovers nonexplosion directly. Multiple linkage classes and molecularity above two remain open.

metadata.title: Strong Tree-Childness Is a Sharp Generic-Identifiability Boundary for Level-2 Jukes-Cantor Networks
metadata.description:
Reticulate evolutionary histories encode hybridization, recombination, and lateral transfer, but such histories are scientifically recoverable from sequence data only when distinct networks induce distinguishable site-pattern distributions. We determine this information limit for binary, LSA-rootable, already-simple semi-directed strongly tree-child level-2 networks under the paper's one-step reticulation-preserving convention and the open four-state Jukes–Cantor model. A source-relative full-dimensional regular stochastic containment occurs if and only if the labelled reduced bridge trees agree and every pair of corresponding blobs is labelled-isomorphic or differs by ordinary triangle redirection. Hence no proper one-sided generic containment exists, and an exact generic distribution determines a unique topology modulo that redirection. Fourier cut ranks recover the bridge tree, while positive rank-one factorizations recover only projective local tensors modulo the full incidence-scaling group; physical bridge multipliers are not identified. A graph-to-algebra classification of cycle and theta factors, together with marginal submersions and coherent bounded probes, reconstructs arbitrary subdivisions.

The boundary is sharp even without triangles. For every n ≥ 4 we construct two triangle-free networks that are weakly but not strongly tree-child, nonisomorphic, and not triangle-related, yet whose open JC images share a regular relatively open subset of full dimension 2n + 1. A second triangle-containing family exhibits a distinct pendant-transfer mechanism. All finite-atlas, class-membership, Fourier-equality, sign, and Jacobian claims are supported by exact primary and separately implemented replay certificates.

metadata.title: An exceptional four-dimensional unitary Hecke Yang–Baxter operator: a five-word Pauli–Clifford normal form
metadata.description: We give a five-word real Pauli–Clifford normal form for an explicit 16 by 16 unitary Yang–Baxter operator in the exceptional Hecke class [exp(i pi/3), 1/2, 4]. Scalar partial traces yield the Markov trace and a faithful localization of the H_n(3,6) Jones–Wenzl tower; a direct obstruction proves that four is the minimum local dimension. C. Galindo and E. C. Rowell, Unitary Yang–Baxter Operators: Towards a Classification, arXiv:2608.16865v1, independently obtained the same existence and strict-localization conclusion, with four smallest in Lechner's exceptional family, through a quaternionic twisted-group-algebra construction. This revision gives an intrinsic quaternionic factorization and an exact local-unitary comparison to the opposite of their literal Family III operator, then extends the comparison to an all-strand unitary equivalence. It derives a scalar Turaev enhancement whose trace invariant is twice the HOMFLYPT specialization at (i,i), with finite-image, Clifford-frame, branched-cover, and exact polynomial-time consequences. The record includes the manuscript, five exact verification routes, deliberate failure tests, frozen output, checksums, source audits, chronology, and submission metadata.

metadata.description:
Simultaneous amplification beyond fitness three halves — preprint v1.0.0

This public preprint proves a strict improvement to the known robust simultaneous-amplification interval for Birth–death and death–Birth updating.

Main theorem

Let

[ P(R)=R^6-8R^5+22R^4-30R^3+21R^2-6R+1 ]

and let

[ R_{\mathrm{hyb}}=1.5028569127905696\ldots ]

be its unique root in (3/2,151/100). The paper constructs one explicit fitness-independent family of finite connected undirected weighted graphs that eventually amplifies every fixed 1<r<R_hyb under both update rules. Consequently,

[ R_{\mathrm{sim}}\ge R_{\mathrm{hyb}}>3/2. ]

This exactly refutes the proposed threshold R_sim=3/2.

Construction and certificates

The family combines a clique core, ordinary hub leaves, and dilute internally heavy K_2 satellites. The release includes:

  • the complete manuscript and deterministic PDF;
  • exact labelled-chain lumping and transition checks;
  • exact rational coefficient identities;
  • Sturm and tangency certificates for the algebraic threshold;
  • a second independently derived asymptotic proof path;
  • the exact counterexample excluding every graph-independent convex affine endpoint separator;
  • hostile-audit and page-by-page PDF QA records; and
  • a one-command replay script, plus a pinned clean-archive bootstrap.

Scope

metadata.title: A four-parameter family of reversible three-species mass-action continua without a common factor
metadata.description:
Version 2 DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21753997

We determine an exact four-dimensional rate family on one fixed reversible, one-linkage, three-species mass-action support with ten complexes and ten reversible pairs. Every positive member has full stoichiometric rank and vanishes on the same compact positive algebraic ellipse. The positive rate set is a rational relatively open polyhedral cone, while a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the family has geometrically coprime coordinate polynomials.

A primitive positive integer specialization has largest rate 10296 and rate sum 52464, simultaneously optimal for both objectives within the fixed support and conic-preserving integral family. Exact certificates also give radical decompositions for both displayed specializations and a transverse-stability classification for the immutable Version 1 ellipse.

  • fixed support: three species, ten complexes, ten reversible pairs, one linkage class;
  • conic-remainder matrix: 21 x 20, rank 16, nullity 4;
  • coordinate gcd: geometrically one on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the constrained family;
  • verification: four exact replay layers, including a separately implemented v2 audit.

The continuum-preserving family has codimension sixteen in the ambient twenty-dimensional rate space. This is not a claim of persistence under arbitrary rate perturbations or global minimality of the ten-complex support.

Scoped PDFs, exact source, verifier archives, checksums, and one-command reproduction instructions are attached to the GitHub Version 2 release. The automatic archive here is the tagged monorepo source.

DOI scope. Zenodo repository-level concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21753404 groups unrelated releases from the AlecKriebel/Math monorepo and is not a paper-specific all-versions DOI. Cite this version using 10.5281/zenodo.21753997.

Priority scope. Boros, Craciun, and Yu already supplied a positive-dimensional fixed-support same-curve rate family, but every member retains a common scalar factor. A targeted primary-source audit through 1 August 2026 found no earlier weakly reversible fixed-support positive family preserving a compatibility-class continuum while being generically free of a coordinate common factor within that family. This is a conservative, nonexhaustive audit conclusion. The release is unreviewed; a DOI is not a correctness certificate.

metadata.title: AlecKriebel/Math: No universal death–birth amplifier v1.0.0
metadata.description:
No universal death–birth amplifier, v1.0.0

This release publishes the fixed-graph obstruction and its exact verification materials.

Main results

  • Every fixed finite loopless directed weighting with positive incoming degree is eventually death–birth suppressing, or its full death–birth chain exactly ties the complete graph.
  • For complete directed support, the first strong-selection deficit is an explicit sum of squares over incoming weight columns.
  • Every nonuniform positive weighted triangle suppresses death–birth fixation for every beneficial fitness.
  • The same all-beneficial-fitness classification holds for the full symmetric 1+3 and 2+2 complete-support families on four vertices.
  • Eventual amplification at every fixed fitness requires support degree to diverge in probability; a separate theorem excludes unequal-degree dense finite-type blow-ups under its stated hypotheses.

Scope

The release rules out one population threshold that works uniformly for every beneficial fitness. It does not settle the reversed quantifier order in which the population threshold may depend on fitness. The unrestricted six-edge weighted K_4, the diffuse asymptotically regular regimes, and the optimal simultaneous-amplification interval remain open.

Reproducibility

make paper1 rebuilds all exact checks and the manuscript. The released run used Python 3.14.6, SymPy 1.14.0, and Tectonic 0.16.9. Release assets include the typeset paper, editable manuscript source, the complete reproduction tree, and a SHA-256 manifest.

The manuscript and internal hostile audits are AI-assisted and have not undergone external specialist peer review.

metadata.title: Minimum Bell-Setting Complexity for Qubit POVM–PVM Separation Integrity Manifest
metadata.description:
This unreviewed preprint establishes a minimum-setting classification for fixed-qubit POVM–PVM separation in bipartite Bell experiments. For every two-input-per-party architecture with arbitrary finite, input-dependent output alphabets, the shared-randomness convex hull of qubit POVM behaviors equals the shared-randomness convex hull of fixed-qubit PVM behaviors. The paper also gives an explicit rational 3×2 Bell functional with an exact qubit-POVM strategy whose value exceeds a global analytic qubit-PVM upper bound. Consequently, 3×2, up to exchanging the parties, is the minimum input architecture for such a linear Bell-functional separation.

The equality concerns convexified behavior sets. It does not assert equality of the raw nonconvex strategy images, same-state simulation, or operator-level projective simulability of individual POVMs.

Generative-AI systems were used substantively throughout the mathematical exploration, derivation, adversarial proof analysis, software development, literature support, and manuscript preparation. The human author accepts responsibility for all claims, citations, and released artifacts. At the time of this version’s initial release, the manuscript had not undergone independent expert peer review.

Source release: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/releases/tag/qubit-povm-pvm-minimum-settings-v1.1.0
